### Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why | Alternative Rejected | Trade-off |
|----------|--------|-----|---------------------|-----------|
| "+N months" computation | Every effect via cumulative re-run of `shocks.runway` on lever-adjusted (income, spending, buffer, oneOff) | The judge formula is the single source of truth; a shortcut formula (e.g. `buffer/gap` deltas) can drift at the `no_shortfall`/cap branches | Direct formula on gap | One runway call per lever step; trivial cost (integer math, <1 ms budget) |
| Lever sizing base | Levers sized from **profile** numbers (S, F, P, insurance), never shocked ones | Judge hand-checks use part-1 metrics; shock additions (bills +15%, extra monthly) are not discretionary and must not be "cut away" by a lever | Size against shocked spending | Under a bills shock the trim lever cannot absorb the increase; that is the honest answer |
| Discretionary margin | `disc = max(0, S − (F + P))` with `trim_discretionary` spending down exactly to the F+P cut floor | Matches the E2-approved cut floor definition; zero when no margin exists (explicit "no margin" row) | Percent-of-spending cuts (arbitrary) | Accounts with tiny margins (68257: disc = $9.19) show +0.0 months; that is a true finding, not a bug |
| Levers below the floor | `defer_loan` (−P) and `shop_insurance` (−insurance) deliberately go under F+P and are labeled as structural moves ("simulated counterfactual") | Deferral is real bank hardship practice with P exact in the data; insurance renegotiation is bounded by `insurance_cents` | Forbidding all floor breaches (would kill 2 of 3 levers) | The printed floor line must say "ordinary cuts stop at F+P; labeled structural moves go under it on purpose" |
| Standing-orders lever | **REJECT** | `standing_orders.csv` is not in `profiles.json`; adding it means an E1 schema change (exact-key loader, verify.py, frozen fixtures) and the source is an undated snapshot | Precompute per-account order sums in E1 | Lever set misses "cancel discretionary standing orders"; acceptable, recorded in decisions |
| Secondary-buffer lever | **REJECT** | No cross-account linkage exists (transfers land at partner banks outside the dataset); `balance_series` is the same single account's money | "Restore buffer to 12-month peak" (not a lever the customer can pull) | `buffer_depleted` accounts show all levers at +0.0; surfaced as an honest plan line instead |
| Goal target | Keep `3 × S` starter with `6 × S` stretch chips (GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS = 6 = the EI duration) | Standard emergency-fund guidance is 3 to 6 months of spending; the challenge's own twist runs 6 months at 55%, so 3 is starter and 6 is storm-ready; both printed as "our definition" | 6 × S only (less reachable; weakens the goal story) or 3–6 range formula (two headline numbers) | A judge preferring 6 × S sees it as the stretch chip row |
| Months to target | Keep scaffold `ceil(target / contribution)` from zero (EXTEND verdict; keeps E2 invariant) + printed "savings on hand" disclosure line | Changing it breaks the approved E2 plan numbers and the invariant in the test plan | Netting B into months (see Q1) | Two facts on the card (months from zero, buffer on hand) instead of one netted number |
| Python twin | **RESTORE, test-side only** (no build.py/verify.py coupling) | Data Use rubric (25%) rewards "every plan number cross-checked by two independent implementations against frozen goldens"; cross-language drift is the recurring failure mode and `golden_fixtures.json` parity is the established remedy; drafts already exist so cost is ~150 lines | Abandon + delete (zero cost, loses the drift guard and the rubric argument) | Every future plan rule change needs two edits; a missed edit is a failing pytest, which is the point. Time-boxed fallback: abandon if the TS side slips (Q2) |
| Golden fixture file | New frozen `scripts/engine/golden_plans.json` (do not touch `golden_fixtures.json`) | `golden_fixtures.json` is frozen E1 hand computation; plans need their own frozen table with workings | Extend `golden_fixtures.json` | One more fixture file; matches the established pattern |
| ConsoleView/store | Zero changes; `buildPlanText` composes planMath internally | The one seam (`plan={derivation.plan}`) survives E3's concurrent mount work untouched; no merge conflicts | ConsoleView computes planMath in its useMemo and passes parts down | `buildPlanText` is a slightly larger composer; acceptable since it is already the "arithmetic lives here" layer |

### Interfaces

All money fields integer cents; all month counts integers; sentinels `MONTHS_UNREACHABLE = -1`, `CUT_NOT_APPLICABLE = -1` (existing).

```ts
// src/lib/planMath.ts (new)

/** The 6 month stretch cushion, the EI duration in the challenge twist. */
export const GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS = 6            // sits beside GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS = 3
export const GOAL_MILESTONE_MONTHS = [1, 2, 3, 6] as const

export interface GoalMilestone {
  monthsOfSpending: number        // k in "k months of typical spending"
  amountCents: number             // k x S, integer cents
  monthsToReach: number           // ceil(k x S / contribution), or MONTHS_UNREACHABLE
  isGoal: boolean                 // k === GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS
  isStretch: boolean              // k === GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS
}
export function goalMilestones(incomeCents: number, spendingCents: number): GoalMilestone[]

export type LeverId = 'shop_insurance' | 'trim_discretionary' | 'defer_loan'

/** One lever's explicit effect on the shocked cash flow, integer cents. */
export interface LeverEffect {
  incomeDeltaCents: number        // 0 for every E4 lever
  spendingDeltaCents: number      // <= 0: every E4 lever cuts monthly spending
  bufferDeltaCents: number        // 0 for every E4 lever (no data backed buffer lever)
}

export interface Lever {
  id: LeverId
  label: string                   // plain words, the ladder row title
  caveat: string                  // honesty tag, "simulated counterfactual, ..." (dash clean)
  effect: LeverEffect
}

export interface LeverInputs {
  // Shocked numbers, straight from ShockResult (never re-derived here).
  shockedIncomeCents: number
  shockedSpendingCents: number
  oneOffCents: number
  bufferCents: number             // profile.buffer_cents (pre one-off), for the re-run
  // Profile numbers the levers are sized from (judge part-1 metrics).
  fixedCostsCents: number         // F
  loanPaymentCents: number        // P (0 when no running loan)
  insuranceCents: number          // median insurance
  typicalSpendingCents: number    // S
}

export interface LeverStep {
  lever: Lever
  incomeAfterCents: number        // cumulative, integer cents
  spendingAfterCents: number      // cumulative, integer cents
  bufferLeftCents: number         // bufferCents - oneOffCents (unchanged by E4 levers)
  runwayAfter: RunwayAnswer       // shocks.runway re-run from scratch after this step
  plusDeciMonths: number          // cumulative vs shocked baseline, tenths, >= 0
  stepDeciMonths: number          // marginal vs previous step, tenths, >= 0
}

export interface LeverLadder {
  baseline: RunwayAnswer          // the shocked runway each step improves on
  steps: LeverStep[]              // application order, only levers the data supports
}
export function leverLadder(input: LeverInputs): LeverLadder
```

**Lever semantics (the contract table):**

| Order | id | Availability | Effect (integer cents) | Honesty label (caveat) | Floor interaction |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `shop_insurance` | `insuranceCents > 0` | `spendingDelta = −insuranceCents` | "simulated counterfactual: premiums re-shopped, upper bound of renegotiation" | Goes under F+P on purpose (premium itself is renegotiated) |
| 2 | `trim_discretionary` | `disc = max(0, S − (F+P)) > 0` | `spendingDelta = −disc` | "simulated counterfactual: all discretionary spending above the fixed cost floor trimmed" | Lands exactly on F+P |
| 3 | `defer_loan` | `loanPaymentCents > 0` | `spendingDelta = −loanPaymentCents` | "simulated counterfactual: hardship deferral, the payment resumes later and interest cost is not modeled" | Goes under F+P on purpose (P itself is deferred) |

Composition rule: `leverLadder` filters to available levers in order 1→2→3, applies effects **cumulatively** (`spendingAfter = max(0, shockedSpending + Σ deltas)`; the `max(0, ...)` is a defensive guard, asserted unreachable on all fixtures), and re-runs `shocks.runway(bufferCents, oneOffCents, shockedIncome, spendingAfter)` per step. Display rules for the +N column (in planText, dash clean): both finite → `"+X.X months"`; baseline finite and after `no_shortfall` → `"clears the shortfall (120+ months)"`; baseline `buffer_depleted` → `"+0.0 months (buffer depleted: restore a positive balance first)"`.

  highlight: 'goal' | 'stretch' | 'plain'
}

export interface LeverRow {
  id: LeverId
  label: string
  caveat: string
  effectCents: number            // magnitude of the monthly spending cut
  runwayAfter: string            // formatDeciMonths(runwayAfter.deciMonths, state)
  plusLabel: string              // per display rules above
  plusDeciMonths: number         // raw, for tests
  stepDeciMonths: number         // raw, for tests
}

export interface PlanText {
  goal: string[]          // E2 lines + cut/status lines (numbers from goalPlan)
  goalChips: GoalChip[]   // milestone chips, goal block
  backup: string[]        // E2 lines + cut floor / horizon definition lines
  levers: LeverRow[]      // the ladder table rows
  definitions: string[]   // the "our definition" disclosure strip
}
// signature unchanged:
export function buildPlanText(profile, result, twist, band): PlanText

## QUESTIONS FOR USER
*(Each has a recommended default; implementation proceeds on the defaults unless overridden.)*

1. **Months to goal: count the buffer already saved?** The scaffold counts new contributions from zero (e.g. "67 months" even when the buffer already covers part of the target). **Default: keep the from-zero headline (preserves the E2 plan-text invariant) and add one printed disclosure line "Savings on hand: $B (x.x months of spending), not counted in the months above."** Alternative: net the buffer into months-to-target (more impressive number, but changes a plan number vs E2 behavior and needs judge hand-checks to use the printed formula).
2. **Python twin: restore or abandon `scripts/engine/plans.py`?** **Default: RESTORE as a test-side twin** (fix the broken `scale_cents` import, finish goal+backup+levers, add `test_plans.py` mirroring the TS goldens over a new shared `golden_plans.json`). No build/verify coupling. Fallback if the TS side slips: delete the file and record "abandoned" in decisions.md (5 minutes). Rationale in §Technology Decisions.
3. **Insurance lever size.** "Re-shop insurance premiums" is only derivable as the account's median `insurance_cents`. **Default: include it at the full median, labeled "simulated counterfactual, upper bound of renegotiation"**, available only when `insurance > 0` (all five golden fixtures have insurance = 0, so it is unit-tested synthetically). Alternative: halve it (arbitrary) or drop it.
4. **Ladder order: free moves first?** **Default: shop insurance (free, reversible) → trim discretionary (lifestyle) → defer loan (future interest cost)**, applied cumulatively. Alternative: descending magnitude (demo-impact order).

## Architecture: Plan Engine (Goal Math + Backup Levers) - Phase E4 of E7

### Overview

E4 extends the already scaffolded `src/lib/planMath.ts` (goalPlan/backupPlan, reviewed EXTEND) with the phase's headline feature: an ordered, cumulative **lever ladder** whose "+N months" effects are always computed by re-running `shocks.runway` on lever-adjusted integer-cents cash flows, never a fresh formula. `planText.ts` becomes the render layer over planMath outputs (chips, lever rows, printed definition lines), and `PlanCard` renders them; `ConsoleView` and the store are untouched.

### Phase Scope

- **Covers:** goal milestone chips + "our definition" disclosure lines (closing the E2 review item requiring printed horizon/cut-floor definitions), the lever model (`shop_insurance`, `trim_discretionary`, `defer_loan`) with per-lever honesty labels and +N months effects, the Python twin decision, and the shared golden plan fixtures.
- **Depends on (unchanged):** E1 `AccountProfile` artifact fields (I, F, S, B, H, P, `insurance_cents`), E2 `shocks.ts` (`applyTwist`, `runway`, `scaleCents`) and `verdict.ts`.
- **Explicitly out of scope:** anything in `src/components/weather/*`, `src/lib/forecast.ts`, and the ConsoleView mount layout (E3, in progress). No store changes (E6 owns `consoleStore`).
- **The single integration seam with E3:** `PlanCard` continues to receive one `PlanText` object via `<PlanCard plan={derivation.plan} />` in ConsoleView's `useMemo` derivation. E4 grows the `PlanText` type and PlanCard's internals; the ConsoleView JSX line where plan output renders is byte-identical before and after E4. E3's WeatherPanel mounts above `PlanCard` at that same call site without conflict.

### Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why | Alternative Rejected | Trade-off |
|----------|--------|-----|---------------------|-----------|
| "+N months" computation | Every effect via cumulative re-run of `shocks.runway` on lever-adjusted (income, spending, buffer, oneOff) | The judge formula is the single source of truth; a shortcut formula (e.g. `buffer/gap` deltas) can drift at the `no_shortfall`/cap branches | Direct formula on gap | One runway call per lever step; trivial cost (integer math, <1 ms budget) |
| Lever sizing base | Levers sized from **profile** numbers (S, F, P, insurance), never shocked ones | Judge hand-checks use part-1 metrics; shock additions (bills +15%, extra monthly) are not discretionary and must not be "cut away" by a lever | Size against shocked spending | Under a bills shock the trim lever cannot absorb the increase; that is the honest answer |
| Discretionary margin | `disc = max(0, S − (F + P))` with `trim_discretionary` spending down exactly to the F+P cut floor | Matches the E2-approved cut floor definition; zero when no margin exists (explicit "no margin" row) | Percent-of-spending cuts (arbitrary) | Accounts with tiny margins (68257: disc = $9.19) show +0.0 months; that is a true finding, not a bug |
| Levers below the floor | `defer_loan` (−P) and `shop_insurance` (−insurance) deliberately go under F+P and are labeled as structural moves ("simulated counterfactual") | Deferral is real bank hardship practice with P exact in the data; insurance renegotiation is bounded by `insurance_cents` | Forbidding all floor breaches (would kill 2 of 3 levers) | The printed floor line must say "ordinary cuts stop at F+P; labeled structural moves go under it on purpose" |
| Standing-orders lever | **REJECT** | `standing_orders.csv` is not in `profiles.json`; adding it means an E1 schema change (exact-key loader, verify.py, frozen fixtures) and the source is an undated snapshot | Precompute per-account order sums in E1 | Lever set misses "cancel discretionary standing orders"; acceptable, recorded in decisions |
| Secondary-buffer lever | **REJECT** | No cross-account linkage exists (transfers land at partner banks outside the dataset); `balance_series` is the same single account's money | "Restore buffer to 12-month peak" (not a lever the customer can pull) | `buffer_depleted` accounts show all levers at +0.0; surfaced as an honest plan line instead |
| Goal target | Keep `3 × S` starter with `6 × S` stretch chips (GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS = 6 = the EI duration) | Standard emergency-fund guidance is 3 to 6 months of spending; the challenge's own twist runs 6 months at 55%, so 3 is starter and 6 is storm-ready; both printed as "our definition" | 6 × S only (less reachable; weakens the goal story) or 3–6 range formula (two headline numbers) | A judge preferring 6 × S sees it as the stretch chip row |
| Months to target | Keep scaffold `ceil(target / contribution)` from zero (EXTEND verdict; keeps E2 invariant) + printed "savings on hand" disclosure line | Changing it breaks the approved E2 plan numbers and the invariant in the test plan | Netting B into months (see Q1) | Two facts on the card (months from zero, buffer on hand) instead of one netted number |
| Python twin | **RESTORE, test-side only** (no build.py/verify.py coupling) | Data Use rubric (25%) rewards "every plan number cross-checked by two independent implementations against frozen goldens"; cross-language drift is the recurring failure mode and `golden_fixtures.json` parity is the established remedy; drafts already exist so cost is ~150 lines | Abandon + delete (zero cost, loses the drift guard and the rubric argument) | Every future plan rule change needs two edits; a missed edit is a failing pytest, which is the point. Time-boxed fallback: abandon if the TS side slips (Q2) |
| Golden fixture file | New frozen `scripts/engine/golden_plans.json` (do not touch `golden_fixtures.json`) | `golden_fixtures.json` is frozen E1 hand computation; plans need their own frozen table with workings | Extend `golden_fixtures.json` | One more fixture file; matches the established pattern |
| ConsoleView/store | Zero changes; `buildPlanText` composes planMath internally | The one seam (`plan={derivation.plan}`) survives E3's concurrent mount work untouched; no merge conflicts | ConsoleView computes planMath in its useMemo and passes parts down | `buildPlanText` is a slightly larger composer; acceptable since it is already the "arithmetic lives here" layer |

### Interfaces

All money fields integer cents; all month counts integers; sentinels `MONTHS_UNREACHABLE = -1`, `CUT_NOT_APPLICABLE = -1` (existing).

```ts
// src/lib/planMath.ts (new)

/** The 6 month stretch cushion, the EI duration in the challenge twist. */
export const GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS = 6            // sits beside GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS = 3
export const GOAL_MILESTONE_MONTHS = [1, 2, 3, 6] as const

export interface GoalMilestone {
  monthsOfSpending: number        // k in "k months of typical spending"
  amountCents: number             // k x S, integer cents
  monthsToReach: number           // ceil(k x S / contribution), or MONTHS_UNREACHABLE
  isGoal: boolean                 // k === GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS
  isStretch: boolean              // k === GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS
}
export function goalMilestones(incomeCents: number, spendingCents: number): GoalMilestone[]

export type LeverId = 'shop_insurance' | 'trim_discretionary' | 'defer_loan'

/** One lever's explicit effect on the shocked cash flow, integer cents. */
export interface LeverEffect {
  incomeDeltaCents: number        // 0 for every E4 lever
  spendingDeltaCents: number      // <= 0: every E4 lever cuts monthly spending
  bufferDeltaCents: number        // 0 for every E4 lever (no data backed buffer lever)
}

export interface Lever {
  id: LeverId
  label: string                   // plain words, the ladder row title
  caveat: string                  // honesty tag, "simulated counterfactual, ..." (dash clean)
  effect: LeverEffect
}

export interface LeverInputs {
  // Shocked numbers, straight from ShockResult (never re-derived here).
  shockedIncomeCents: number
  shockedSpendingCents: number
  oneOffCents: number
  bufferCents: number             // profile.buffer_cents (pre one-off), for the re-run
  // Profile numbers the levers are sized from (judge part-1 metrics).
  fixedCostsCents: number         // F
  loanPaymentCents: number        // P (0 when no running loan)
  insuranceCents: number          // median insurance
  typicalSpendingCents: number    // S
}

export interface LeverStep {
  lever: Lever
  incomeAfterCents: number        // cumulative, integer cents
  spendingAfterCents: number      // cumulative, integer cents
  bufferLeftCents: number         // bufferCents - oneOffCents (unchanged by E4 levers)
  runwayAfter: RunwayAnswer       // shocks.runway re-run from scratch after this step
  plusDeciMonths: number          // cumulative vs shocked baseline, tenths, >= 0
  stepDeciMonths: number          // marginal vs previous step, tenths, >= 0
}

export interface LeverLadder {
  baseline: RunwayAnswer          // the shocked runway each step improves on
  steps: LeverStep[]              // application order, only levers the data supports
}
export function leverLadder(input: LeverInputs): LeverLadder
```

**Lever semantics (the contract table):**

| Order | id | Availability | Effect (integer cents) | Honesty label (caveat) | Floor interaction |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `shop_insurance` | `insuranceCents > 0` | `spendingDelta = −insuranceCents` | "simulated counterfactual: premiums re-shopped, upper bound of renegotiation" | Goes under F+P on purpose (premium itself is renegotiated) |
| 2 | `trim_discretionary` | `disc = max(0, S − (F+P)) > 0` | `spendingDelta = −disc` | "simulated counterfactual: all discretionary spending above the fixed cost floor trimmed" | Lands exactly on F+P |
| 3 | `defer_loan` | `loanPaymentCents > 0` | `spendingDelta = −loanPaymentCents` | "simulated counterfactual: hardship deferral, the payment resumes later and interest cost is not modeled" | Goes under F+P on purpose (P itself is deferred) |

## Frontend Implementation: Phase E3 Weather Viz

### Design Plan
- **Palette**: band hues from the existing `cp` scale (critical `#ff6a4d`, storm `#f4b740`, watch `#8b7cf6`, fair `#39c2e0`, clear `#35d0ae`), grounds `#070c18`, parchment `#e9e0c9`. One color source: `band.tailwind` classes flow through `currentColor` into SVG slots, band left rules, and labels, so badge and strip can never disagree.
- **Typography**: `wx-font-display` (ui-monospace stack) for labels, pins, horizon note; `wx-font-body` (system-ui) for glyphs and thresholds; utility uppercase tracked caps for tags.
- **Layout**: full width panel between the shock grid and PlanCard: header (eyebrow, title, storm front caption), `wx-cliff-wrap` containing the strip SVG plus the HTML cliff overlay on the shared slot grid, history honesty note, band key grid.
- **Signature element**: the forecast strip itself, a weather map of one person's money: muted recorded balance line left of the storm front, band-colored month slots (color + glyph + tooltip) with the projection polyline, landfall pin printing the exact headline figure, dashed worst case continuation to its second pin, and a printed horizon note.

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/lib/forecast.ts` | NEW: `projectForecast`, `monthLabel`, anchors asserted, adaptive horizon, integer ceil landfall, display-only EI cliff block |
| `src/lib/forecast.test.ts` | NEW: 26 tests, I1 to I5, both 4,500-profile sweeps, golden fixtures |

## Staged delivery protocol (mandatory)
Write and test in stages; each stage's files must be ON DISK with green targeted tests before the next begins. Never hold multiple stages in memory.
Stage 1: planMath.ts additions + unit goldens/invariants. Stage 2: golden_plans.json + planMath.golden.test.ts. Stage 3: planText.ts + PlanCard.tsx + index.css + tests. Stage 4: Python twin (shocks.py scale_cents, plans.py finish, test_plans.py). Stage 5: dashScan registration + full gates.

## Hard constraints
- Integer cents throughout; no float decides a branch. Runway math ONLY via shocks.runway (every lever "+N months" = difference of two shocks.runway answers; acceptance check includes grepping for any other runway formula in planMath/planText).
- No em/en dashes, minus sign equivalents, double or spaced hyphens in ANY new string or comment (numeric minus in formatted money allowed).
- ZERO diff to src/components/console/ConsoleView.tsx and src/state/consoleStore.ts (E3 just landed there; the only seam is the existing <PlanCard plan={derivation.plan} /> call site, which must remain byte-identical).

Only mention trails if you can verify any usage in this repo (check `git branch -a` for trail branches); if none, mention the toolchain capability without claiming this project used it.

## Writing requirements (hard)
- NO em dashes, en dashes, minus signs, double hyphens, or spaced hyphens anywhere (the repo convention; an automated dash scan enforces this on src and the team applies it to docs).
- Sentence case, plain verbs, user-side framing, no marketing fluff.
- Frame it as honest engineering practice: what problem each feature solved here (e.g. graph-first discovery prevented redundant exploration across concurrent agent sessions; --head vs worktree told agents what was committed vs in flight; checkpoints tied commits to the session that made them; token accounting kept multi-agent cost visible).
- 150 to 350 words for the section. A short command list or tight bullets are fine if the README uses that style elsewhere.
- Do not mention internal agent names (00-planner etc.) unless the README already does; describe the multi-agent workflow generically.

```markdown
## Use of Entire

Entire was in place before this repo's first commit. The Friday dress rehearsal in `docs/entire-rehearsal.md` proved the toolchain end to end in a sandbox repo in 10 minutes, and `entire enable -y --agent opencode` ran before commit `1300799 chore: initial repo with Entire enable files and Tangerine dataset manifest`. The enable files (`.entire/settings.json`, `.entire/.gitignore`, `.opencode/plugin/entire.ts`) and the Graph agent guide (`.entire/agent-guide.md`) ship in the repo.

- **Every session starts with a Graph query.** `.entire/agent-guide.md` is injected into AGENTS.md, so every agent session auto-loads the rule that the first action on a code task must be a Graph query. `entire graph query` finds code for a description, `entire graph def` shows a symbol, `entire graph neighbors` lists callers and callees (`--direction in` or `out`), and `entire graph impact` gives the blast radius before a symbol changes; the guide also covers Graph diff, commit, and checkpoint for semantic comparisons of revisions. The `--head` flag queries the committed tree while the default reads uncommitted edits, so parallel sessions could tell committed code from work in flight.
- **The index reports what it skipped.** `entire graph health` reports index state (the rehearsal measured 71 source files indexed in 1204 ms), and query-time Coverage lines name the files the indexer skipped, typically minified or generated data, rather than leaving a silent gap.
- **Every commit names its session.** Commits made during agent sessions carry an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer naming the session checkpoint, checkpoint snapshots are stored as commits under `refs/entire/checkpoints/`, and `entire checkpoint explain HEAD` reconstructs a commit's intent and transcript.
- **Token cost stays visible.** `entire session tokens` reports per-session input, cache read, output, and API calls, and `entire tokens profile --json` aggregates usage across checkpoints, which keeps a multi-agent workflow's cost visible. `entire trail create` offers title-branched trails for review; this project stayed on `main`.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e46afc7d6ffezYxKaoUbg5IJfi" state="completed" description="Design E6 judge mode">
All context gathered. Here is the Phase E6 architecture. Two genuine contradictions surfaced (Esc semantics, rehearsal form), so I am asking them first with defaults, and the design below proceeds on those defaults.

## QUESTIONS FOR USER
- Q1: Esc semantics conflict: `consoleStore.ts` documents "Esc clears the lookup query" while the E6 brief says "Esc = clear selection". Recommended default: layered dismiss, Esc cancels an open typed-shock gate first, then clears the lookup query, then resets the whole console (query is already empty at that point, so the last step equals clear selection plus clear twist). This matches the between-judges ritual and needs no new store action.
- Q2: Rehearsal form: an in-app timed dock (small component driving the real console through 5 scripted steps) vs a printed script only (section of the paper sheet). Recommended default: in-app dock with the printed script as the named cut line if the hour runs short (the script data module ships either way).

---

## Architecture: Judge Mode (E6) - Phase 6 of 7

### Overview
E6 turns the console into a live judging instrument: one authoritative keyboard map exported from `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` and wired by a thin window-level adapter hook, an edge-account guard rebuilt to read the E1 profile flags (with contextual copy for the layoff-on-pensioner case), a lean scripted rehearsal dock over 5 frozen golden-fixture accounts, and a one-page printable judge sheet in `public/` as the laptop-dead fallback. All rules stay pure functions in `src/lib`; components only wire listeners and markup, and the adapter fires exactly one existing atomic store action per keystroke.

### Phase Scope
Covers: keyboard shortcuts and their context rules, edge-account guards and operator script lines, rehearsal mode and its data, paper fallback artifact. Connects to: E2 (store actions and DOM seams `id="account-lookup"`, `data-preset`, `type="button"` are consumed, not changed; the reserved key map comment in `consoleStore.ts` is superseded by a pointer to the judgeMode registry), E5 (Atlas above console, `id="atlas"` / `id="console"`; the single window listener works across both sections), E4 (reads `planMath`/`planText`/`PlanCard` for context only, zero edits to those files or README.md), E7 (ReceiptBadge untouched; only a receipt link slot in the bar is possible later). Out of scope: any store action changes, any shock math, any E4 plan content.

### Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why | Alternative Rejected | Trade-off |
|----------|--------|-----|---------------------|-----------|
| Key map source of truth | One `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS` table in `src/lib/judgeMode.ts`; `consoleStore` comment points at it | The brief names judgeMode as owner; one table means the bar, the tests, and the sheet cannot drift | Keeping two maps with a sync comment | The E2 comment wording (Esc, arrows) is superseded; recorded in decisions.md |
| Key set | Exactly the reserved map: `1`-`4`, `r`, `Shift+R`, `/`, `Esc`, `N` (9 bindings) | Reserved map is the approved contract; arrows removed (they conflicted with the map and with text selection via Shift+arrows) | Keeping ArrowLeft/ArrowRight walking | Account browsing loses keyboard stepping; lookup typing and N cover the ritual |
| Modifier policy | Reject ctrl/meta/alt always; `shiftKey` allowed only for bindings with `allowShift` (only `Shift+R`) | Shift alone never triggers browser shortcuts; `Shift+R` needs it; `Shift+4` types `$` so numbers cannot collide | Blanket modifier reject (killed Shift+R) | Caps Lock `R` also fires reset-all; documented, harmless |
| Listener placement | Pure `resolveJudgeKey` in lib + `useJudgeShortcuts` window listener mounted in `App` | Window scope works across Atlas and console (E5 layout); pure rules unit test without DOM; layering holds | Listeners in ConsoleView (misses Atlas focus, remount churn); listeners in the store module (DOM in state layer) | One global listener must own the focus guard carefully |
| Typed-shock interplay | While `typedStatus` is `reading` or `pending`, only `Esc` resolves; text-entry focus suppresses everything except `Esc` | `applyPreset` would silently `retireTypedParse` and drop the judge's sentence chips; typing `1` in the lookup is an id digit, not a shortcut | Allowing resets during the gate | The confirm button is auto-focused (a button), so the gate-open rule is required, not just the focus rule |
| Guard source | Read `profile.flags` (E1 artifact) instead of re-deriving thresholds | E1 flags are verified field-by-field by `scripts/engine/verify.py`; kills the dead `GUARD_MIN_ROWS = 6` and its wrong message | Keeping `rowCount < 18` re-derivation in TS | Guard trusts the artifact; drift is caught by the existing engine verify, not duplicated in TS |
| Guard placement | Full messages in the judge-facing `JudgeBar` strip (operator), short chips near the verdict (`GuardChips`) | Operator needs the sentence, judges need the glance; two renders of one pure `GuardReport` via `useEdgeGuard` | Chips inside ShockPanel/PlanCard (merge risk with E4) | Chips sit under `cp-grid`, a few pixels from the badge rather than inside it |
| N picker | Pure `pickRandomAccount` with a "safe demo" pool, injectable `rng` | Never embarrasses the operator; deterministic under test and rehearsal | Uniform random over 4500 ids | Extreme accounts are unreachable via N (still typed by judges, guarded) |
| Rehearsal | Pure `rehearsal.ts` script + lean `RehearsalDock` with stopwatch | The live ritual is timing muscle memory; the data module survives the UI cut | Full game-like scoring, persistence | No history or scoring beyond a per-step green/amber/red label |
| Paper fallback | `public/judge-sheet.html`, standalone, `@media print`, linked from the runbook | Ships with Pages, prints offline, needs no build step; runbook "Offline booth" row expects everything bundled | `docs/` markdown (not printable to one page without tooling); generated PDF in repo (binary churn) | Hand-copied numbers from `golden_fixtures.json`; an optional test pins them |

### Authoritative Key Table (ships in the bar, the sheet, and the tests)

| Key | event.key | Action | Effect | Context rules |
|-----|-----------|--------|--------|---------------|
| `1` | `1` | twist preset 1 | `applyPreset('layoff')` | Suppressed in text entry and while the typed gate is open |
| `2` | `2` | twist preset 2 | `applyPreset('cost_spike')` | Same |
| `3` | `3` | twist preset 3 | `applyPreset('emergency_repair')` | Same |
| `4` | `4` | twist preset 4 | `applyPreset('combo')` | Same |
| `r` | `r` | reset twist, keep account | `resetTwist()` | Same |
| `Shift+R` | `R` | reset everything | `resetAll()` | Same; the only binding tolerating shift. Caps Lock `R` also fires it |
| `/` | `/` | focus lookup | `#account-lookup`.focus(), preventDefault (Firefox quick find) | Suppressed in text entry and while the gate is open |
| `Esc` | `Escape` | layered dismiss | gate open: `cancelTypedShock()`; else query non-empty: `setQuery('')` (+ blur); else selected or shocked: `resetAll()`; else no-op | Active everywhere, including text entry (the only key exempt from the focus guard) |
| `N` | `n` | pseudo-random account | `selectAccount(pickRandomAccount(bundle))` | Suppressed in text entry and while the gate is open; key repeat ignored |

Esc layered rule (the Q1 default): it dismisses the innermost layer first, so the operator can never lose a typed sentence to a stray keypress, and between judges two presses (or one when no query) return the console to the empty state. This supersedes the `consoleStore` comment wording.

### Guard Copy Table (no dash glyphs anywhere)

| Flag id | Fires when | Chip label | Operator message (bar) | Operator script line (rehearsal) |
|---------|-----------|------------|------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `unknown_account` | id missing or not in `bundle.byId` | unknown id | Account id is not in the loaded profile set | "That id is not in the 4,500 account index, let me retype it." |
| `pensioner` (idle) | `flags.pensioner` | pension income | Pension income account: money in is pension, not wages | "Income here is pension, so the money in line reads differently." |
| `pensioner` (layoff twist live) | `flags.pensioner && twist.jobLoss` | pension vs layoff | Layoff twist simulated against pension income: this account has no wage to lose, read the verdict as a stress test | "Good catch: this customer's income is pension, so the layoff card is a stress test on fixed income. Their real risk is bills up, not job loss." |
| `zero_income` | `flags.zero_income` | zero income | Zero income: money in is 0, so the layoff and EI framing does not apply | "Money in is zero here, so I read the shock as a spending side stress." |
| `thin_history` | `flags.thin_history` (row_count under 18, E1 definition) | thin history | Thin history: fewer than 18 monthly rows, so the baseline medians rest on a short window | "Short history, so I treat the baseline as low confidence." |
| `negative_buffer` | `flags.negative_buffer` | negative buffer | Savings buffer is below zero: the baseline already reads 0.0 months of runway | "Buffer is already below zero, so the plan is recovery first." |
| `defaulted_loan` | `flags.defaulted_loan`, message varies on `loan.status` | defaulted loan | status D: Loan in arrears (status D): the account still pays a loan it is behind on. status B: Loan defaulted and closed (status B): no payment runs, so the loan levers do not apply | D: "This loan is running and in arrears, so deferral is exactly the intervention." B: "This loan already defaulted and closed, so there is no payment to defer." |
| `no_loan` | `loan_payment_cents === 0` | no loan | No running loan payment: the loan deferral lever does not apply | "No loan payment here, so I skip the loan lever and say why." |
| `zero_household_bills` | `household_bills_cents === 0` | zero bills | Household bills are 0: a bills shock cannot move this account | "Bills are zero here, so a rent shock cannot land; I would swap to the repair card." |

Rules: flags are advice, never gates (`selectAccount` accepts any known id regardless of flags, the hard constraint "any account must work" is untouched). Canonical order is `GUARD_FLAG_ORDER`, the pensioner message variant is decided by the live twist, and every message keeps the repo no-dash content rule (a `judgeMode.test.ts` case already scans for dash code points; keep it). This table backs the shipped `docs/devpost.md` claim: thin history, negative buffer, zero bills, and missing loans all flag before a judge finds them.

### Rehearsal Spec

Format: scripted dry run, 5 steps, timed, no stakes, driven through the real store so the operator practices the actual keystrokes. Target: 2.0 s from step reveal to "Answered" click (`REHEARSAL_TARGET_MS`); labels `fast` / `ok` / `slow` at 2 s / 4 s.

| Step | Account | Why this account | Twist | Expected flags | Expected read |
|------|---------|------------------|-------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | `68257` | Golden fixture: odd median, running loan C, clean | `layoff` (1) | none | Fair skies 9.8 months falls to Storm warning 1.8 months |
| 2 | `23838` | Golden fixture: half cent tie in I, `no_shortfall` branch | `cost_spike` (2) | none | Verdict stays Clear, buffer absorbs |
| 3 | `98952` | Golden fixture: pensioner, no loan | `layoff` (1) | `pensioner` (layoff variant), `no_loan` | Stress-test framing, loan lever skipped |
| 4 | `49900` | Golden fixture: thin history (17 rows) and zero income | `combo` (4) | `thin_history`, `zero_income` | Caveat spoken before the number |
| 5 | `42988` | Golden fixture: defaulted loan status D, negative buffer | `emergency_repair` (3) | `defaulted_loan` (D variant), `negative_buffer` | Baseline already 0.0, recovery plan |

Coverage: all five E1 flags fire at least once, all four presets fire once except `layoff` (twice, needed for the pensioner variant), every runway branch appears across the fixtures. Candidate selection criteria (recorded for any future re-pick): ids come from `scripts/engine/golden_fixtures.json`, which is hand-verified and pinned by both pytest and vitest; `rehearsal.test.ts` asserts each step's id exists in the shipped `profiles.json` with exactly the expected flags, so artifact drift fails a test and names the step. If a rebuild ever invalidates an id, re-pick from `meta.edge_flag_counts` smallest buckets first (`zero_income` 14, `negative_buffer` 23, `defaulted_loan` 45, `thin_history` 377, `pensioner` 740), preferring fixture-frozen ids so the paper sheet example stays pinned.

UI (`RehearsalDock`): opened from a toggle in `JudgeBar`; shows step n of 5, the judge card sentence (from `presetById`), the script line, a "Run step" button (selects the account and applies the preset via the store), and an "Answered" button that stops the stopwatch and prints the verdict label. Closing resets the counter. No persistence, no network, no score history.

Cut line (Q2 default): if the hour runs short, cut `RehearsalDock.tsx` and keep `rehearsal.ts` plus a printed script block in the judge sheet. The data module is cheap and the sheet prints it.

### Paper Fallback Spec (`public/judge-sheet.html`)

Purpose: the rehearsed fallback when the laptop dies or the venue network stalls (runbook risk table "Offline booth" expects everything bundled locally with fixture labels; `docs/devpost.md` promises a graceful fallback). Standalone HTML, inline CSS, `@media print` sized to one US Letter page, no build step, no JS. Linked from `docs/competition-day-runbook.md` (Sunday demo row and the Offline booth fallback cell) and printable from the live site (`/judge-sheet.html`). Readme linking is deliberately out of scope (concurrent agent owns README.md).

Sections, in order:
1. **Header**: "Resilience Weather Station, judge sheet", competition name, "synthetic demo data label applies to cached fixture figures".
2. **The six definitions**: I, F, S, B, H, P exactly as `docs/tangerine-challenge.md` lines 52 to 59.
3. **Runway formula and rounding**: the branch formula (challenge doc lines 63 to 69), ROUND_HALF_UP to 1 decimal, cap at 120.0.
4. **Worked example** (numbers hand-copied from `scripts/engine/golden_fixtures.json` account `68257`, whose "steps" block is visible workings): I = 650,326c, S = 716,084c, B = 643,785c, H = 430,672c, P = 284,493c, gap = 65,758c, baseline deci = (20 x 643785 + 65758) // (2 x 65758) = 98, so 9.8 months. Layoff card: income_after = round(0.55 x I) = 357,679c, gap_after = 716,084 - 357,679 = 358,405c, deci = (20 x 643785 + 358405) // (2 x 358405) = 18, so 1.8 months. Fair skies becomes Storm warning.
5. **Verdict bands**: the five `verdict.ts` bands with their threshold strings (critical: buffer gone or under 1.0 month; storm warning 1.0 to 2.9; watch 3.0 to 5.9; fair skies 6.0 to 11.9; clear 12.0 and up or no shortfall).
6. **Twist card arithmetic**: `income_after = 0.55 x I` (layoff), `spending_after = S + 0.15 x H` (bills up 15%), `one_off_costs = 1.0 x S` (furnace), combo is layoff plus bills; duration is display only.
7. **Guard one-liners**: the chip labels plus one phrase each from the guard copy table.
8. **Key table**: the authoritative 9 rows.
9. **Rehearsal script**: the 5 steps (account, card, expected flags), so the drill survives a dead laptop.

Content rules: no em dash, en dash, minus sign, or double hyphen anywhere (use `x`, `+`, and words); money shown in cents and dollars; every figure traceable to `golden_fixtures.json` 68257 or to `verdict.ts` / `shockPresets.ts` literals. Optional `judge-sheet` test (cut line 2) reads the file in vitest and asserts the worked example figures and the no-dash rule.

All context gathered. Here is the Phase E6 architecture. Two genuine contradictions surfaced (Esc semantics, rehearsal form), so I am asking them first with defaults, and the design below proceeds on those defaults.

## QUESTIONS FOR USER
- Q1: Esc semantics conflict: `consoleStore.ts` documents "Esc clears the lookup query" while the E6 brief says "Esc = clear selection". Recommended default: layered dismiss, Esc cancels an open typed-shock gate first, then clears the lookup query, then resets the whole console (query is already empty at that point, so the last step equals clear selection plus clear twist). This matches the between-judges ritual and needs no new store action.
- Q2: Rehearsal form: an in-app timed dock (small component driving the real console through 5 scripted steps) vs a printed script only (section of the paper sheet). Recommended default: in-app dock with the printed script as the named cut line if the hour runs short (the script data module ships either way).

---

## Architecture: Judge Mode (E6) - Phase 6 of 7

### Overview
E6 turns the console into a live judging instrument: one authoritative keyboard map exported from `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` and wired by a thin window-level adapter hook, an edge-account guard rebuilt to read the E1 profile flags (with contextual copy for the layoff-on-pensioner case), a lean scripted rehearsal dock over 5 frozen golden-fixture accounts, and a one-page printable judge sheet in `public/` as the laptop-dead fallback. All rules stay pure functions in `src/lib`; components only wire listeners and markup, and the adapter fires exactly one existing atomic store action per keystroke.

### Phase Scope
Covers: keyboard shortcuts and their context rules, edge-account guards and operator script lines, rehearsal mode and its data, paper fallback artifact. Connects to: E2 (store actions and DOM seams `id="account-lookup"`, `data-preset`, `type="button"` are consumed, not changed; the reserved key map comment in `consoleStore.ts` is superseded by a pointer to the judgeMode registry), E5 (Atlas above console, `id="atlas"` / `id="console"`; the single window listener works across both sections), E4 (reads `planMath`/`planText`/`PlanCard` for context only, zero edits to those files or README.md), E7 (ReceiptBadge untouched; only a receipt link slot in the bar is possible later). Out of scope: any store action changes, any shock math, any E4 plan content.

### Component Breakdown

| Component | Responsibility | File |
|-----------|---------------|------|
| Key registry + resolver | Single authoritative key table, pure context-aware resolution, modifier policy | `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` (rewrite) |
| Edge guard | Pure guard report from `AccountProfile` flags + live twist context + unknown id | `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` (rework `edgeGuard`) |
| Random account picker | Pure "safe demo" pool and seeded pick for the N key | `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` (new `pickRandomAccount`) |
| Rehearsal script | Pure data: 5 steps over the golden fixture accounts, timer verdict | `src/lib/rehearsal.ts` (new) |
| Dispatcher + key listener | Thin DOM adapter: maps `JudgeAction` to existing store actions and focus effects | `src/components/judge/useJudgeShortcuts.ts` (new) |
| Guard derivation hook | One `useMemo` over `{bundle, selectedId, twist}` calling `edgeGuard`, shared by bar and chips | `src/components/judge/useEdgeGuard.ts` (new) |
| Judge chips | Judge-facing short-label chips near the verdict, full message on hover/aria | `src/components/judge/GuardChips.tsx` (new) |
| Judge bar (extend) | Renders the 9 bindings as buttons via the shared dispatcher; rehearsal toggle; paper sheet link | `src/components/judge/JudgeBar.tsx` (extend) |
| Rehearsal dock | Timed dry run UI: run step, answer button, elapsed vs 2.0 s target | `src/components/judge/RehearsalDock.tsx` (new) |
| App shell | Mounts `useJudgeShortcuts`, `JudgeBar` (bottom), `RehearsalDock` | `src/App.tsx` (extend) |
| Console shell | Mounts `GuardChips` as one new sibling line after `cp-grid` | `src/components/console/ConsoleView.tsx` (one line) |
| Paper sheet | Standalone printable one page: definitions, formula, bands, worked example, guards, keys | `public/judge-sheet.html` (new) |
| Store comment | Reserved key map block replaced by a pointer to `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS` | `src/state/consoleStore.ts` (comment only) |

### Data Flow

```
window keydown (App mounts useJudgeShortcuts once)
  -> adapter: isTextEntry(target)? isComposing? repeat?   (DOM facts only)
  -> resolveJudgeKey(event, context)                      [pure, src/lib/judgeMode.ts]
       context = { inTextEntry, typedGateOpen }
  -> JudgeAction | null
  -> dispatchJudgeAction(action)   (same function serves JudgeBar button clicks)
       twist n      -> useConsole.applyPreset(SHOCK_PRESETS[n-1].id)
       reset_twist  -> useConsole.resetTwist()
       reset_all    -> useConsole.resetAll()
       focus_lookup -> document.getElementById('account-lookup').focus()
       dismiss      -> cancelTypedShock() | setQuery('') | resetAll()   (layered)
       random       -> pickRandomAccount(bundle, {rng}) -> selectAccount(id)
  -> store update (one atomic action per keystroke, E2 contract intact)
  -> ConsoleView derivation useMemo (unchanged: applyTwist, verdictBand, forecast, plan)
  -> useEdgeGuard(): edgeGuard({profile, jobLossActive, knownAccountIds})
       -> GuardChips (chips row under cp-grid) + JudgeBar guard strip (full messages)
RehearsalDock "Run step" -> same store actions (selectAccount + applyPreset), stopwatch local
```

### File Structure

| `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` | Registry, resolver, guard, picker, copy tables | Rewrite: 9-binding `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS`, `resolveJudgeKey`, `edgeGuard` over `AccountProfile`, `pickRandomAccount`, delete `GUARD_MIN_ROWS`, `account_prev/next`, old flag set |
| `src/lib/judgeMode.test.ts` | Unit tests | Rewrite to the new registry, context matrix, guard copy, picker determinism |
| `src/lib/rehearsal.ts` | `REHEARSAL_SCRIPT`, `REHEARSAL_TARGET_MS`, `rehearsalVerdict` | New |
| `src/lib/rehearsal.test.ts` | Coverage + artifact pinning | New |
| `src/components/judge/useJudgeShortcuts.ts` | `useJudgeDispatcher`, `useJudgeShortcuts` | New |
| `src/components/judge/useEdgeGuard.ts` | `useEdgeGuard` shared derivation | New |
| `src/components/judge/GuardChips.tsx` | Chip row near verdict | New |
| `src/components/judge/RehearsalDock.tsx` | Timed dry run panel | New |
| `src/components/judge/JudgeBar.tsx` | Bar | Extend: props `onToggleRehearsal`, `rehearsalOpen`, `paperHref`; trailing link + toggle button |
| `src/components/judge/JudgeBar.test.ts` | Bar tests | Extend: 9 bindings, toggle, paper link |
| `src/components/judge/judgeShortcuts.smoke.test.ts` | jsdom adapter smoke (style of `console.smoke.test.ts`) | New |
| `src/App.tsx` | Shell | Extend: `useJudgeShortcuts()`, `<JudgeBar>` bottom bar with `onAction={dispatch}`, `<RehearsalDock>` |
| `src/components/console/ConsoleView.tsx` | Console shell | One line: `<GuardChips guard={useEdgeGuard()} />` after `cp-grid` (or extract to a prop-free child if the E4 merge conflicts) |
| `src/state/consoleStore.ts` | Store | Comment only: reserved map block becomes "see `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS` in src/lib/judgeMode.ts" |
| `public/judge-sheet.html` | Printable fallback | New: standalone inline-CSS one pager |
| `docs/competition-day-runbook.md` | Runbook | Add the sheet link to the Sunday demo row and the "Offline booth" risk fallback cell |
| `docs/judge-sheet.test.ts` (optional, in `src/`) | Asserts sheet numbers | New, cut line 2 |

### Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why | Alternative Rejected | Trade-off |
|----------|--------|-----|---------------------|-----------|
| Key map source of truth | One `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS` table in `src/lib/judgeMode.ts`; `consoleStore` comment points at it | The brief names judgeMode as owner; one table means the bar, the tests, and the sheet cannot drift | Keeping two maps with a sync comment | The E2 comment wording (Esc, arrows) is superseded; recorded in decisions.md |
| Key set | Exactly the reserved map: `1`-`4`, `r`, `Shift+R`, `/`, `Esc`, `N` (9 bindings) | Reserved map is the approved contract; arrows removed (they conflicted with the map and with text selection via Shift+arrows) | Keeping ArrowLeft/ArrowRight walking | Account browsing loses keyboard stepping; lookup typing and N cover the ritual |
| Modifier policy | Reject ctrl/meta/alt always; `shiftKey` allowed only for bindings with `allowShift` (only `Shift+R`) | Shift alone never triggers browser shortcuts; `Shift+R` needs it; `Shift+4` types `$` so numbers cannot collide | Blanket modifier reject (killed Shift+R) | Caps Lock `R` also fires reset-all; documented, harmless |
| Listener placement | Pure `resolveJudgeKey` in lib + `useJudgeShortcuts` window listener mounted in `App` | Window scope works across Atlas and console (E5 layout); pure rules unit test without DOM; layering holds | Listeners in ConsoleView (misses Atlas focus, remount churn); listeners in the store module (DOM in state layer) | One global listener must own the focus guard carefully |
| Typed-shock interplay | While `typedStatus` is `reading` or `pending`, only `Esc` resolves; text-entry focus suppresses everything except `Esc` | `applyPreset` would silently `retireTypedParse` and drop the judge's sentence chips; typing `1` in the lookup is an id digit, not a shortcut | Allowing resets during the gate | The confirm button is auto-focused (a button), so the gate-open rule is required, not just the focus rule |
| Guard source | Read `profile.flags` (E1 artifact) instead of re-deriving thresholds | E1 flags are verified field-by-field by `scripts/engine/verify.py`; kills the dead `GUARD_MIN_ROWS = 6` and its wrong message | Keeping `rowCount < 18` re-derivation in TS | Guard trusts the artifact; drift is caught by the existing engine verify, not duplicated in TS |
| Guard placement | Full messages in the judge-facing `JudgeBar` strip (operator), short chips near the verdict (`GuardChips`) | Operator needs the sentence, judges need the glance; two renders of one pure `GuardReport` via `useEdgeGuard` | Chips inside ShockPanel/PlanCard (merge risk with E4) | Chips sit under `cp-grid`, a few pixels from the badge rather than inside it |
| N picker | Pure `pickRandomAccount` with a "safe demo" pool, injectable `rng` | Never embarrasses the operator; deterministic under test and rehearsal | Uniform random over 4500 ids | Extreme accounts are unreachable via N (still typed by judges, guarded) |
| Rehearsal | Pure `rehearsal.ts` script + lean `RehearsalDock` with stopwatch | The live ritual is timing muscle memory; the data module survives the UI cut | Full game-like scoring, persistence | No history or scoring beyond a per-step green/amber/red label |
| Paper fallback | `public/judge-sheet.html`, standalone, `@media print`, linked from the runbook | Ships with Pages, prints offline, needs no build step; runbook "Offline booth" row expects everything bundled | `docs/` markdown (not printable to one page without tooling); generated PDF in repo (binary churn) | Hand-copied numbers from `golden_fixtures.json`; an optional test pins them |

### Interfaces

### Authoritative Key Table (ships in the bar, the sheet, and the tests)

| Key | event.key | Action | Effect | Context rules |
|-----|-----------|--------|--------|---------------|
| `1` | `1` | twist preset 1 | `applyPreset('layoff')` | Suppressed in text entry and while the typed gate is open |
| `2` | `2` | twist preset 2 | `applyPreset('cost_spike')` | Same |
| `3` | `3` | twist preset 3 | `applyPreset('emergency_repair')` | Same |
| `4` | `4` | twist preset 4 | `applyPreset('combo')` | Same |
| `r` | `r` | reset twist, keep account | `resetTwist()` | Same |
| `Shift+R` | `R` | reset everything | `resetAll()` | Same; the only binding tolerating shift. Caps Lock `R` also fires it |
| `/` | `/` | focus lookup | `#account-lookup`.focus(), preventDefault (Firefox quick find) | Suppressed in text entry and while the gate is open |
| `Esc` | `Escape` | layered dismiss | gate open: `cancelTypedShock()`; else query non-empty: `setQuery('')` (+ blur); else selected or shocked: `resetAll()`; else no-op | Active everywhere, including text entry (the only key exempt from the focus guard) |
| `N` | `n` | pseudo-random account | `selectAccount(pickRandomAccount(bundle))` | Suppressed in text entry and while the gate is open; key repeat ignored |

Esc layered rule (the Q1 default): it dismisses the innermost layer first, so the operator can never lose a typed sentence to a stray keypress, and between judges two presses (or one when no query) return the console to the empty state. This supersedes the `consoleStore` comment wording.

### Guard Copy Table (no dash glyphs anywhere)

| Flag id | Fires when | Chip label | Operator message (bar) | Operator script line (rehearsal) |
|---------|-----------|------------|------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `unknown_account` | id missing or not in `bundle.byId` | unknown id | Account id is not in the loaded profile set | "That id is not in the 4,500 account index, let me retype it." |
| `pensioner` (idle) | `flags.pensioner` | pension income | Pension income account: money in is pension, not wages | "Income here is pension, so the money in line reads differently." |
| `pensioner` (layoff twist live) | `flags.pensioner && twist.jobLoss` | pension vs layoff | Layoff twist simulated against pension income: this account has no wage to lose, read the verdict as a stress test | "Good catch: this customer's income is pension, so the layoff card is a stress test on fixed income. Their real risk is bills up, not job loss." |
| `zero_income` | `flags.zero_income` | zero income | Zero income: money in is 0, so the layoff and EI framing does not apply | "Money in is zero here, so I read the shock as a spending side stress." |
| `thin_history` | `flags.thin_history` (row_count under 18, E1 definition) | thin history | Thin history: fewer than 18 monthly rows, so the baseline medians rest on a short window | "Short history, so I treat the baseline as low confidence." |
| `negative_buffer` | `flags.negative_buffer` | negative buffer | Savings buffer is below zero: the baseline already reads 0.0 months of runway | "Buffer is already below zero, so the plan is recovery first." |
| `defaulted_loan` | `flags.defaulted_loan`, message varies on `loan.status` | defaulted loan | status D: Loan in arrears (status D): the account still pays a loan it is behind on. status B: Loan defaulted and closed (status B): no payment runs, so the loan levers do not apply | D: "This loan is running and in arrears, so deferral is exactly the intervention." B: "This loan already defaulted and closed, so there is no payment to defer." |
| `no_loan` | `loan_payment_cents === 0` | no loan | No running loan payment: the loan deferral lever does not apply | "No loan payment here, so I skip the loan lever and say why." |
| `zero_household_bills` | `household_bills_cents === 0` | zero bills | Household bills are 0: a bills shock cannot move this account | "Bills are zero here, so a rent shock cannot land; I would swap to the repair card." |

Rules: flags are advice, never gates (`selectAccount` accepts any known id regardless of flags, the hard constraint "any account must work" is untouched). Canonical order is `GUARD_FLAG_ORDER`, the pensioner message variant is decided by the live twist, and every message keeps the repo no-dash content rule (a `judgeMode.test.ts` case already scans for dash code points; keep it). This table backs the shipped `docs/devpost.md` claim: thin history, negative buffer, zero bills, and missing loans all flag before a judge finds them.

### Rehearsal Spec

Format: scripted dry run, 5 steps, timed, no stakes, driven through the real store so the operator practices the actual keystrokes. Target: 2.0 s from step reveal to "Answered" click (`REHEARSAL_TARGET_MS`); labels `fast` / `ok` / `slow` at 2 s / 4 s.

| Step | Account | Why this account | Twist | Expected flags | Expected read |
|------|---------|------------------|-------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | `68257` | Golden fixture: odd median, running loan C, clean | `layoff` (1) | none | Fair skies 9.8 months falls to Storm warning 1.8 months |
| 2 | `23838` | Golden fixture: half cent tie in I, `no_shortfall` branch | `cost_spike` (2) | none | Verdict stays Clear, buffer absorbs |
| 3 | `98952` | Golden fixture: pensioner, no loan | `layoff` (1) | `pensioner` (layoff variant), `no_loan` | Stress-test framing, loan lever skipped |
| 4 | `49900` | Golden fixture: thin history (17 rows) and zero income | `combo` (4) | `thin_history`, `zero_income` | Caveat spoken before the number |
| 5 | `42988` | Golden fixture: defaulted loan status D, negative buffer | `emergency_repair` (3) | `defaulted_loan` (D variant), `negative_buffer` | Baseline already 0.0, recovery plan |

Coverage: all five E1 flags fire at least once, all four presets fire once except `layoff` (twice, needed for the pensioner variant), every runway branch appears across the fixtures. Wording is the pinned `docs/solana.md` contract (unit-tested in the existing `ReceiptBadge.test.ts`, unchanged). 2. The label scopes the claim to the exact artifact; the anchor title says "written at build time ... opens the local evidence file". 3. Links are plain anchors only: the bundled evidence file (base-path aware via `dataBase()`) and the explorer URL (`target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"`). No code ever calls RPC or fetches over the network. 4. A digest honesty test recomputes SHA256 of `public/data/findings.json` and `public/data/model_card.json` and asserts equality with the bundled evidence `payload_sha256`, so a post-freeze artifact rewrite fails `vitest` loudly instead of shipping a stale badge. ### Gate Conditions (design question 4) Adapted from the approved package; all required before the first send: 1. **Root memo confirmed** with explorer link: **already met** (finalized evidence in `scripts/solana/evidence/memo-devnet.json`). Mismatch = treat as gate failure (the anchor no longer describes the shipped artifact). 2. **Re-runs green first** (pivot adaptation of "findings re-run verified green"): `uv run python -m scripts.engine.verify` exit 0, `uv run pytest -q` exit 0, `npx vitest run` exit 0. 3. **60-minute cap** on the whole package (sends, bundling, `ReceiptStamp`, tests, seam). The cut rule when time runs short (gate was green at kickoff): cut receipt 3 first, then receipt 2, then receipt rows (badge + root + tests never cut). In a cap-hit partial state (root bundled, badge live, 2/3 cut) the paragraph **does** land, because that state is a reduced package, not a gate failure; only condition failure at the 4:30 decision line silences the paragraph. ### Write-up Paragraph (design question 5) The approved sentence applies **verbatim** under the pivot (F3 AUC 0.590 is still the declared model limit; `model_card.json` and the findings machinery ship in-repo): > future work: a behavioral score attested on chain could gate a credit line or automate surplus sweeps; not implemented, and the underlying model (F3, AUC 0.590) is not strong enough to gate credit **Target**: `docs/devpost.md`, final line of `### Limits we declare up front` (section 4, around line 104). That file is owned by another session: the orchestrator routes this exact sentence to its owner as a paste instruction (explicitly labeled not built; the sentence's own "future work:" and "not implemented" wording is the label per the approved package). Gate: only if the package shipped per the rules above. ### MLH Solana Track Claim (design question 6) What earns the track: (1) three real, confirmed devnet memo transactions with explorer links over the frozen analysis artifacts (findings root, model card hash, F1 aggregate fingerprint, "aggregates only, no raw rows"); (2) a visible, honest receipt surface on the live site (badge in the verdict card + receipt rows) reading bundled evidence with zero runtime RPC; (3) the bundled evidence files a judge can open and hash-check offline; (4) the labeled not-built future-work sentence. The `docs/devpost.md` checkbox ("select only if the memo anchor confirms with an explorer link before 5:30 PM Sat") is **met** (finalized 2026-11-07T02:47:12Z). Booth Q&A one-liner (the approved rejection rationale): > we anchored the findings themselves on chain because that is the claim that needed the chain; everything else stayed on the honest side of the line. (Check `solana balance` first; 0 + faucet closed = cut 2/3, go to step 4) | | 2 | 0:12 | Receipt 3 per runbook Phase 6: `mkdir -p build`; `uv run python -c "import json; print(json.dumps(json.load(open('public/data/findings.json'))['f1StructuralVsDiscretionary'], sort_keys=True))" > build/f1-aggregate-table.json`; `send_memo.py --file build/f1-aggregate-table.json --prefix "Sheridan Datathon 2026 F1 aggregate fingerprint, aggregates only, no raw rows" --evidence scripts/solana/evidence/memo-devnet-fingerprint.json`; `solana confirm ` | | 3 | 0:18 | `cp` all existing evidence siblings into `public/data/` (root regardless; 2/3 as landed) | | 4 | 0:20 | `src/data/receipts.ts` + `src/data/receipts.test.ts` (guards, mapping, digest honesty) | | 5 | 0:35 | `src/components/console/ReceiptStamp.tsx` + test + `cp-receipt-*` styles appended to `src/index.css` | | 6 | 0:48 | **The seam**: `BaselineCard.tsx` +1 import +1 line. `npx vitest run`, `npx vite build` green (build proves the glob resolves) | | 7 | 0:55 | Route the devpost sentence to the devpost owner; apply the acceptance checklist; land docs (content below) | | 8 | 1:00 | **HARD STOP.** Whatever is green ships; anything else is cut silently | Step F (gate failure): mount `ReceiptStamp` with whatever evidence exists (placeholder if none), no sends, no paragraph, record why in `docs/decisions.md`. ### Test Plan 1. **`src/data/receipts.test.ts`** - `parseChainReceipt`: valid evidence file maps (`matches_local: true` -> verified); `matches_local: false` -> unverified with signature line; malformed shapes -> `null` (placeholder path); missing signature -> "unavailable" wording path. - **Digest honesty**: `readFileSync` + `node:crypto` SHA256 of `public/data/findings.json` equals `ROOT_RECEIPT.payloadSha256`; same for `model_card.json` when its receipt exists; fingerprint evidence self-consistency (`memo_text_on_chain` contains `payload_sha256`, prefix carries "aggregates only, no raw rows"). - Registry: returns only existing files; root-first ordering. 2. **`src/components/console/ReceiptStamp.test.ts`** (renderToString over fixture receipts passed via the `receipts` prop, so tests never fight `import.meta.glob`): - Root present + verified: anchor wraps the badge, contains "Anchored on Solana devnet, verified"; `href` is `/data/memo-devnet.json` (base-path aware via `dataBase()`); explorer anchor has `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`; one row per receipt rendered. - Root absent: renders the placeholder ("no evidence yet") and zero rows. - Dash scan over all rendered strings (content convention). 3. **Guardrails**: existing `ReceiptBadge.test.ts` and `judge/**` tests stay green **unchanged** (they prove E7 did not touch the scaffold); `console.smoke.test.ts` still passes with the seam in place. ### Acceptance Checklist (adapted nine checks) - [ ] Ships inside the 60-minute cap (4:30 PM decision line) - [ ] Zero new runtime network calls (eager glob, no fetch; explorer is a plain anchor) - [ ] Zero scope violations (no wallet UI, no Anchor, no tokens, no 3D, no runtime RPC) - [ ] Consumes only bundled artifacts (`public/data/memo-devnet*.json`) - [ ] Every claim matches the bundled evidence (signature, digest, wording) and the digest honesty test is green - [ ] Deception test: badge and rows read as bundled build-time receipts, never a live write; placeholder when evidence missing - [ ] Single-story test: receipts reinforce the provenance story, no second narrative - [ ] Cut-first rule honored (cut order: receipt 3, receipt 2, rows; badge + root + tests never cut) - [ ] Zero video budget impact - [ ] Collision guard: `judge/ReceiptBadge.tsx` + test byte-identical; coordinate via this doc's seam spec | | `import.meta.glob` over a `public/` path misbehaves in Vite/vitest | Build at step 6 proves it early; fallback order: generated `src/data/receipts.generated.json` copied in the same `cp` step, then `fetch(dataBase() + ...)` with the same parser | | Artifact rewrite after sends (digest drift) | Findings freeze Sat 6 PM; digest honesty test fails `vitest` loudly | | Wallet empty for receipts 2/3 (5000 lamports each; faucet flaky) | `solana balance` check at step 1; zero balance = cut rule, root-only ships | | Badge misread as a live on-chain claim | Pinned wording, scoping label, anchor title, "bundled at build time" note; verified in the deception check | | Devpost sentence drift (F3 AUC 0.590 vs answer key) | Exact sentence routed verbatim; no paraphrase | --- ## Ready-to-land docs content ### `docs/architecture.md` (replace in full) ```markdown # Financial Resilience Engine Architecture Last updated: Sun Nov 08 2026 (Phase E7 design). Status: E1 to E5 shipped. E6 judge mode in flight. E7 (Solana receipt touch) designed and gated, implementation pending. ## Product A financial resilience engine for real bank customers, built for the Tangerine track of the Sheridan Datathon 2026. At judging a judge picks an account_id and a twist card, and the engine runs live in about five minutes: know the customer (I, F, S, B, H, P, gap, runway from the precomputed profile artifact), take a shock (job loss with EI at 55 percent, bills up, one-off repair, or a mix), make a plan (goal plan plus backup levers). The engine is the primary demo surface (full pivot, approved Nov 07 2026); the orbit game and findings-first report are dropped as surfaces, and their machinery is reused internally. ## Hard constraints - Judge definitions are the contract (docs/tangerine-challenge.md). - Integer cents end to end, ROUND_HALF_UP, no float decides a branch. - Deterministic offline artifact: profiles.json is byte identical across builds and carries no timestamps or randomness. - Checksummed sources fail loud (data/tangerine/SHA256SUMS). - Any of the 4500 accounts must work, including the five edge flags. - Content convention: no em dashes, en dashes, minus signs, double hyphens, or spaced hyphens in shipped strings. - Static hosting only. Network allowed as a bonus, never a dependency. - Solana scope lock: memo anchor only. No wallet UI, no Anchor, no tokens, no runtime RPC (docs/decisions.md Nov 06 LOCKED). ## Stack Python 3.14 + uv + pandas + numpy (engine pipeline, pytest); React 19, Vite 6, TypeScript 5.7 strict, Tailwind 3.4, Zustand 5, Vitest (site); GitHub Pages via Actions, base path aware; Entire for graph evidence. ## Phases E1 to E7 - E1 profile precompute (COMPLETE): scripts/engine -> deterministic public/data/engine/profiles.json (meta + 4500 profiles), verified. - E2 console base (COMPLETE): lookup, BaselineCard, ShockPanel, verdict, plan text. - E3 weather viz (COMPLETE): ForecastStrip, WeatherBands, EI cliff. - E4 plan engine (COMPLETE): goal math + backup levers. - E5 Storm Atlas (COMPLETE): population headline + strip-plot drill-down. - E6 judge mode (IN FLIGHT): shortcuts, edge guards, rehearsal, paper fallback (judge/, App.tsx, one ConsoleView line, judge-sheet.html). - E7 Solana A+ touch (GATED, DESIGNED): three build-time devnet receipts over the frozen analysis artifacts (findings.json root memo already sent and finalized; model_card.json hash; F1 aggregate fingerprint), bundled under public/data/memo-devnet*.json, surfaced by one honest receipt badge plus a compact receipt list in the verdict card. ## Data layer data/tangerine/*.csv -> scripts/engine/{load,metrics,shocks,build}.py -> public/data/engine/profiles.json -> scripts/engine/verify.py (naive recompute, drift diff, prints artifact SHA256). Sources: 185,326 + 682 + 4500 rows over 2020-01 to 2025-12. Each profile carries a check_sum over account_id:month rows and money_in cents (mirrored by src/data/checksum.ts). ## Solana receipt layer (E7) Evidence flow: frozen artifact -> scripts/solana/send_memo.py (devnet memo tx, genesis guard, read-back verified) -> scripts/solana/evidence/memo-devnet*.json -> cp to public/data/ -> src/data/receipts.ts (import.meta.glob eager, hand guards) -> ReceiptStamp (console/) -> mounted once in BaselineCard under the provenance line. Zero runtime RPC: the badge reads bundled JSON statically; links (bundled evidence file, Solana explorer) are plain anchors only. ReceiptBadge (judge/) stays props-only and untouched; its wording is pinned by docs/solana.md. Gate conditions, 60 minute cap, cut order, and the skip-silently rule: docs/ideas-tangerine-solana.md adapted in docs/decisions.md (Phase E7). ## Frontend layering 1. Data (src/data): typed loaders with schema validation, checksum mirror, receipts registry. No math, no React. 2. Core (src/lib): pure functions only (shock, verdict, plan, forecast). 3. Views (src/components): ConsoleView shell derives everything once; views format only. Inline money math in a component is a failure. 4. Render (river, scene): presentation only. ## Verification - uv run python -m scripts.engine.build and -m scripts.engine.verify (naive recompute, dash scan, artifact SHA256, exit non zero on drift). - uv run pytest -q: golden fixtures, schema, check_sum recompute, determinism. - npx vitest run: loader guards, shock/plan twins, receipt wording (ReceiptBadge.test.ts), receipt digest honesty (receipts.test.ts), ReceiptStamp markup. - Rule drift guard: verify.py duplicates contract strings on purpose. ## Performance and offline profiles.json under 5 MB, one fetch, parsed once; shock math under 1 ms, no async hop; game budget unchanged (60 fps, dpr 1.5). Everything bundled for offline booths. The Gemini typed-shock path (gated add-on, post E2) is the only code that touches the network and always degrades to preset cards under a 3 second hard timeout; key in VITE_GEMINI_KEY, deleted after Sunday submission. ``` ### `docs/decisions.md` (append) ```markdown ## Nov 08 2026 - Phase E7: Static memo receipts mounted in the verdict card **Context**: the approved gated Solana package (three receipts, static panel, not-built paragraph) was designed for the dropped findings-first site. The pivot to the engine needs the same receipts surfaced in the new single-page layout, without colliding with the concurrent E6 work in judge/, App.tsx, and ConsoleView. **Decision**: keep the approved three receipts exactly (root memo already sent and finalized; model_card.json hash and F1 aggregate fingerprint sent inside the 60 minute cap; no profiles.json chain receipt). The old section E panel folds into a new ReceiptStamp component (console/) that mounts the untouched judge/ReceiptBadge once, in BaselineCard under the provenance line (the one E7 seam), reading public/data/memo-devnet*.json via import.meta.glob eager (zero fetch; missing receipts render the honest placeholder). Links are plain anchors to the bundled evidence and the explorer. Gate conditions unchanged; "findings re-run green" adapts to verify.py + pytest + vitest green; gate failure ships the single memo and skips the paragraph; cap-hit cut order is receipt 3, receipt 2, rows. The approved future-work sentence routes to docs/devpost.md "Limits we declare up front". **Rationale**: the badge is an artifact-level receipt, so provenance-adjacent placement in the baseline verdict card passes the deception test where a hero-verdict stamp would not; the glob keeps the design build-safe in every gate state; keeping judge/ byte-identical removes the only real merge risk. **Trade-offs**: the chain attests the frozen analysis, not the engine artifact (checkable offline via verify.py instead); the panel is a compact row list rather than a section; the JudgeBar receipt slot stays reserved for post-freeze. ```

7. `AGENTS.md` still lists E6 as "Not started"; it was not in my file list, so I left it for the orchestrator to flip.
