# Financial Resilience Engine Architecture

Last updated: Sun Nov 08 2026 (phases E1 to E7 all complete).
Status: E1 profile precompute, E2 console base, E3 weather viz, E4 plan
engine, E5 Storm Atlas, E6 judge mode, and E7 Solana receipt touch all
shipped, reviewed PASS, and committed. The district cartogram and rain
gauge shipped as an E5 extension on the five verdict bands.

## Product

A financial resilience engine for real bank customers, built for the
Tangerine track of the Sheridan Datathon 2026. At judging a judge picks
an `account_id` and a twist card, and the engine runs live in about five
minutes: know the customer (I, F, S, B, H, P, gap, runway from the
precomputed profile artifact), take a shock (job loss with EI at 55
percent, bills up, one-off repair, or a mix), make a plan (goal plan
plus backup levers). The one minute pitch opens with the Storm Atlas:
the runway distribution across all 4,500 accounts, then one click drills
into any account for the live twist. The engine is the primary demo
surface (full pivot, approved Nov 07 2026); the orbit game and
findings first report are dropped as surfaces, and their machinery is
reused internally.

## Hard constraints

- Judge definitions are the contract (docs/tangerine-challenge.md).
- Integer cents end to end, ROUND_HALF_UP, no float decides a branch.
- Deterministic offline artifact: profiles.json is byte identical across
  builds and carries no timestamps or randomness.
- Checksummed sources fail loud (data/tangerine/SHA256SUMS).
- Any of the 4500 accounts must work, including the five edge flags.
- One weather vocabulary: src/lib/verdict.ts owns the five bands
  (critical, storm warning, watch, fair skies, clear) over integer deci
  months (10, 30, 60, 120). The seven state ladder was deleted in E5
  and must not be reintroduced (AGENTS.md coordination note, user
  decision Nov 08).
- Honest sentences: scenario wording derives from the same Twist object
  the math ran (stormAtlas.shockedAtlasScenario).
- Content convention: no em dashes, en dashes, minus signs, double
  hyphens, or spaced hyphens in shipped strings. verify.py scans the
  artifact and dashScan.test.ts scans the site strings.
- Static hosting only. Network allowed as a bonus, never a dependency.
  The Gemini typed shock path is the only network code and degrades to
  preset cards under a 3 second timeout.
- Solana scope lock: memo anchor only. No wallet UI, no Anchor, no
  tokens, no runtime RPC (docs/decisions.md Nov 06 LOCKED).

## Stack

- Python 3.14 + uv + pandas + numpy for the offline engine pipeline;
  pytest for tests. Modules are header style, snake_case, type hinted.
- React 19, Vite 6, TypeScript 5.7 strict, Tailwind 3.4, Zustand 5,
  Vitest for the site.
- GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions, base path aware.
- Entire for graph queries, checkpoints, and the build trail.

## Phases E1 to E7 (all complete)

- E1 profile precompute: scripts/engine writes
  public/data/engine/profiles.json (meta plus 4500 profiles), verified
  by naive recompute, five golden fixtures, deterministic builds.
- E2 console base: account lookup, baseline card, shock presets plus
  sliders, verdict badge, plan text; consoleStore with the key map
  delegated to JUDGE_SHORTCUTS.
- E3 weather viz: forecast projection (src/lib/forecast.ts), storm
  front, landfall pin agreeing exactly with the headline runway,
  verdict band colors, EI cliff overlay labeled beyond the answer key.
- E4 plan engine: goal math (3x starter, 6x stretch chips, definition
  strip) plus the ordered lever ladder (shop_insurance,
  trim_discretionary, defer_loan), every +N months a difference of two
  shocks.runway re-runs, goldens in scripts/engine/golden_plans.json
  asserted by both vitest and pytest (test side Python twin in
  scripts/engine/plans.py).
- E5 Storm Atlas: population headline quoting accounts under 3.0 months
  of runway (1 percent baseline, 10 percent under the laid off twist),
  strip plot with one dot per account on a band aligned axis, drill
  down via selectAccount, bank wide scenario mode; weatherState.ts
  deleted in the fold. Extension (concurrent session): district storm
  cartogram and population rain gauge, public/data/engine/atlas.json
  precomputed on the five verdict bands by scripts/engine/atlas.py.
- E6 judge mode: one authoritative JUDGE_SHORTCUTS table (1 to 4, r,
  Shift + R, slash, Esc layered dismiss, N safe random account), edge
  guards reading E1 flags (inform, never gate), five step rehearsal
  dock over golden fixture accounts, public/judge-sheet.html printable
  fallback linked from the runbook.
- E7 Solana touch: three build time devnet memos (findings.json root
  5YPxwK9, model_card.json hash 3BJiraS5, F1 aggregate fingerprint
  Q7evLcRb, aggregates only) bundled under public/data/, surfaced by
  ReceiptStamp in BaselineCard reading bundled evidence via
  import.meta.glob (zero runtime network); ReceiptBadge wording pinned
  to docs/solana.md; digest honesty tests recompute artifact SHA256s.

## Data layer

```
data/tangerine/*.csv (checksums in SHA256SUMS)
    -> scripts/engine/load.py      (verify, integer cent parse, grouping)
    -> scripts/engine/metrics.py   (pure I, F, S, B, H, gap, flags)
    -> scripts/engine/shocks.py    (pure runway function, scale_cents)
    -> scripts/engine/build.py     (meta + profiles + atlas, deterministic)
    -> public/data/engine/profiles.json  (4500 profiles, about 4.7 MB)
    -> public/data/engine/atlas.json      (district precompute, five bands)
    -> scripts/engine/verify.py    (naive csv recompute, drift diff, SHA256)
```

- Sources: monthly_summary.csv (185,326 rows), loans.csv (682),
  accounts.csv (4,500), districts.csv, over 2020-01 to 2025-12.
- Provenance: each profile carries a check_sum over account_id:month
  rows and money_in cents, recipe in pipeline_lib.checksum mirrored by
  src/data/checksum.ts; the receipt stamp says recorded, never
  reverified in the browser.

## Solana receipt layer (E7)

Evidence flow: frozen artifact -> scripts/solana/send_memo.py (devnet
memo tx, genesis guard, read back verified) ->
scripts/solana/evidence/memo-devnet*.json -> copied to public/data/ ->
src/data/receipts.ts (import.meta.glob eager, hand guards) ->
ReceiptStamp (console/) -> mounted once in BaselineCard under the
provenance line. Zero runtime RPC: the badge reads bundled JSON
statically; links (bundled evidence file, Solana explorer) are plain
anchors only. Gate conditions, cap, cut order, and the skip silently
rule live in docs/ideas-tangerine-solana.md plus the Phase E7 decisions
record. The future work sentence is in docs/devpost.md "Limits we
declare up front".

## Judge mode (E6)

One authoritative keyboard table (JUDGE_SHORTCUTS in
src/lib/judgeMode.ts) drives the bar, the tests, and the printable
judge sheet: 1 to 4 apply the twist presets, r resets the twist,
Shift + R resets everything, slash focuses the account lookup, Esc
dismisses layer by layer (typed gate, then query, then the whole
console), N opens a pseudo random safe demo account. A window level
adapter (src/components/judge/useJudgeShortcuts.ts) owns the DOM facts
(text entry focus, typed gate open, key repeat) and fires exactly one
existing consoleStore action per keystroke; all rules stay pure and
unit tested in src/lib.

Edge guards read the E1 profile flags plus two numeric rules (no
running loan, zero household bills) and one contextual rule (pensioner
under a live layoff twist): they inform the operator in the judge bar
and the judges as chips near the verdict, and they never block an
account selection. Rehearsal is a timed five step dry run over the
golden fixture accounts (src/lib/rehearsal.ts, RehearsalDock), and
public/judge-sheet.html is the one page printable fallback (formula,
verdict bands, worked example from fixture 68257, twist arithmetic,
guards, keys) linked from the competition day runbook.

## Frontend layering

1. Data (src/data): typed loaders with schema validation, checksum
   mirror, receipts registry. No math, no React.
2. Core (src/lib): pure functions only (shocks, verdict, planMath,
   planText, forecast, stormAtlas, atlasPlot, judgeMode, rehearsal).
   Integer cents, never React.
3. Views (src/components): console, weather, atlas, judge. One
   derivation pass in ConsoleView; inline money math in a component is
   a review failure.
4. Render: presentation only.

Load once, memoize: profiles.json is fetched a single time and parsed
once per session. App mounts the Atlas section above the console
(id="atlas", id="console") and the JudgeBar as a sticky bottom bar.

## Verification

- uv run python -m scripts.engine.build and -m scripts.engine.verify
  (independent naive recompute, dash scan, artifact SHA256, exit non
  zero on drift; profiles.json sha256 9ec428bf1a78b35703aa3d36311d4ee0
  61eac7fbd1176cfcbf111acc5c40a858).
- uv run pytest -q: golden fixtures, plan goldens, atlas conservation,
  schema, check_sum recomputation, determinism.
- npx vitest run: loader guards, shock/plan/forecast twins over shared
  goldens, 4500 profile cross checks, atlas conservation, headline
  honesty, receipt wording and digest honesty, judge key matrix, dash
  scan (589 tests at last run).
- Rule drift guard: verify.py duplicates contract strings on purpose.

## Performance and offline

profiles.json under 5 MB, one fetch, parsed once; shock math under 1 ms
per account; the atlas population pass about 2 ms per twist change in
one useMemo. Everything bundled for offline booths; network allowed as
a bonus, never a dependency (Gemini typed input is the sole exception
with a 3 second abort to preset cards).

verdict bands, worked example from fixture 68257, twist arithmetic,
guards, keys) linked from the competition day runbook.

## Frontend layering

1. Data (src/data): typed loaders with schema validation, checksum
   mirror, receipts registry. No math, no React.
2. Core (src/lib): pure functions only (shocks, verdict, planMath,
   planText, forecast, stormAtlas, atlasPlot, judgeMode, rehearsal).
   Integer cents, never React.
3. Views (src/components): console, weather, atlas, judge. One
   derivation pass in ConsoleView; inline money math in a component is
   a review failure.
4. Render: presentation only.

Load once, memoize: profiles.json is fetched a single time and parsed
once per session. App mounts the Atlas section above the console
(id="atlas", id="console") and the JudgeBar as a sticky bottom bar.

- uv run python -m scripts.engine.build and -m scripts.engine.verify
  (independent naive recompute, dash scan, artifact SHA256, exit non
  zero on drift; profiles.json sha256 9ec428bf1a78b35703aa3d36311d4ee0
  61eac7fbd1176cfcbf111acc5c40a858).
- uv run pytest -q: golden fixtures, plan goldens, atlas conservation,
  schema, check_sum recomputation, determinism.
- npx vitest run: loader guards, shock/plan/forecast twins over shared
  goldens, 4500 profile cross checks, atlas conservation, headline
  honesty, receipt wording and digest honesty, judge key matrix, dash
  scan (589 tests at last run).
- Rule drift guard: verify.py duplicates contract strings on purpose.

## Performance and offline

profiles.json under 5 MB, one fetch, parsed once; shock math under 1 ms
per account; the atlas population pass about 2 ms per twist change in
one useMemo. Everything bundled for offline booths; network allowed as
a bonus, never a dependency (Gemini typed input is the sole exception
with a 3 second abort to preset cards).

Rewrite/refresh it as the actual submission story. Format: Markdown with LaTeX math support allowed. Structure and tone should follow the project README (read README.md first: plain, honest, engineer voice, sentence case). Content grounded in the actual project (verify each against the repo: AGENTS.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/decisions.md, docs/reviews.md, docs/findings.md, README.md, docs/tangerine-challenge.md):
- Inspiration: the Tangerine challenge itself (resilience rewired; a "weather forecasting system" for personal finance), the judging ritual (random account id plus surprise twist card, answered live), and the ask: can a bank customer see whether they survive a shock, and what saves them.
- The question we asked (Discovery): how resilient are real account holders actually? e.g. "what share of accounts would survive a month without income" and the shipped finding: 1 percent (60 of 4,500) sit under 3 months of runway at baseline, and the same population under the laid off twist (EI at 55 percent) jumps to 10 percent (435 of 4,500). What we did: precomputed the judge's exact answer-key metrics for all 4,500 accounts, built a live stress-test console with preset and custom shocks, and attached prescriptive plans. What we found: the storm-zone multiplier (10x under one twist), plus per-account stories (a defaulted-loan account whose buffer is already negative, a pensioner where the layoff card is a stress test not a fact, thin-history accounts whose medians rest on a short window). Verify these against the atlas tests and the guard copy before printing numbers.
- How we built it: integer-cents pipeline (Python, uv, pandas) producing a deterministic offline artifact verified by an independent naive recompute; TypeScript twins of the same formulas pinned by shared golden fixtures asserted in BOTH pytest and vitest (cross-language drift becomes a failing test); React console/atlas/judge surfaces with one derivation pass; every claim traceable through provenance check_sums and the dash-scan content rule; Entire graph-first workflow for concurrent multi-agent development.
- Challenges we faced: answer-key exactness (rounding rules a judge can hand-check: medians over all rows, half-up ties, integer tenths of a month); hostile random accounts (edge flags guarded, never gated); a vocabulary conflict resolved by deleting a parallel 7-state ladder so every surface shares one band vocabulary; a stalled agent session cured with staged disk checkpoints; offline booth discipline (everything bundled, network only as a bonus, Gemini gated with a 3 second abort); honest-deception discipline (recorded vs verified provenance, beyond-the-answer-key overlays labeled, receipts reading bundled evidence with zero runtime RPC).
- LaTeX: where math genuinely helps (the runway formula), use LaTeX, e.g. runway = buffer_left / gap with the branch rules, and lever +N months as a difference of two runway evaluations: $\Delta m = m_{runway}(after) - m_{runway}(before)$. Keep it light and correct.
- Limits we declare up front: PRESERVE the existing E7 future-work sentence verbatim (do not touch it), and keep any existing honest limits that are still true; drop limits that were fixed.

## Task 2: Generative AI question
Find where the Devpost form's AI question is handled in docs/devpost.md (grep for "generative", "AI model", "Gemini", "N/A"). If there is a placeholder/section for "Did you implement a generative AI model or API in your hack this weekend? If so, how and why did you use it? If not, mark your response as N/A", fill the ANSWER (we DID implement one): how = typed natural-language shock input: a judge types a sentence like "laid off and rent up 15%", a strict JSON responseSchema maps it to the app's twist fields (income factor, bills percent, one-off months, duration), a mandatory confirm gate applies it to state, 3 second AbortSignal timeout falls back to preset cards, key via VITE_GEMINI_KEY never printed; why = the twist card is spoken language, not sliders; letting a judge speak the shock removes UI friction in the 3 minute live demo while the engine's math never touches the model (the model only fills the same typed twist struct the presets fill, so every number still comes from the deterministic integer-cents engine). Verify the actual behavior in src/lib/shockParse.ts, src/components/console/TypedShock.tsx, and the docs/decisions.md Gemini record before writing (model id, endpoint, schema details: only what the code/docs actually say). If the answer slot does not exist, add it in the section where form answers live (read the file structure first to place it correctly).
- If the file has a paste-map or placeholder table referencing these answers, update the relevant rows.

## Hard rules
- No em/en dashes, minus sign equivalents, double or spaced hyphens anywhere you write (numeric minus in formatted money allowed). The E7 sentence and any existing quoted material keep their exact bytes.
- Every number verifiable in the repo; note your verification sources in the report.
- Keep the doc's existing structure conventions (numbered sections, paste-map style).

Report: sections changed with before/after summaries, the exact AI answer text, verification sources for each number, and a dash-glyph grep result.

=== section 5 video desc ===
  chips before anything moves. The rules engine does the math. The model
  never touches the runway.
- **Accessibility and drama are the same problem.** Severity is carried by
  color and icon and text label, so the storm reads on a projector, on a
  laptop, and to a colorblind judge.

### How we built it

- **Data:** the real anonymized bank dataset (4,500 accounts, 1.06M
  transactions, 185K monthly summaries, 682 loans), credited to the
  PKDD'99 Financial dataset via the CTU Prague Relational Dataset
  Repository.
- **Pipeline:** Python with pandas and numpy, fully vectorized (groupby,
  no per-account loops), integer cents throughout, `uv` for pinned
  dependencies. One pass produces `profiles.json` with the six judge
  metrics (I, F, S, B, H, P) plus a provenance check_sum for every
  number, and two consecutive builds are byte identical. An independent
  verifier recomputes all 4,500 accounts from the raw CSVs with the naive
  csv module (no pandas, no numpy) and diffs field by field, so drift
  fails the build, not the demo.
- **One formula, two languages, frozen fixtures:** the TypeScript twins of
  the Python formulas are pinned by shared golden fixtures asserted in
  both pytest and vitest, plus a cross check over all 4,500 profiles, so
  cross language drift becomes a failing test in either suite. Plans ride
  the same guard: `scripts/engine/golden_plans.json` is asserted from
  both sides.
- **Plans are re-runs, not new math:** each backup lever's "+N months"
  is a difference of two evaluations of the same runway function,
  $$\Delta m = m_{\text{runway}}(\text{after})\,-\,m_{\text{runway}}(\text{before})$$
  so every lever number is hand checkable against the printed formula.
- **Frontend:** React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind. One derivation pass in
  the console view (inline money math in a component is a review
  failure), a pure `verdictBand` function maps runway to five verdict

2. App layout swap + order-dependent test updates.
3. Pixel art assets: pixel sky header (day/storm swap on active band), mascot, chrome pass (borders/shadows/readouts) + new component tests (day/storm swap logic pinned).
4. Cartogram real map: fetch + simplify + name-match + path rendering + tests (all 77 districts accounted for; unmatched listed).

Files per stage; name-match results (77/77 or the fallback list); geometry source URL + final size; contrast ratios for band labels; day/storm swap rule; key-embedded verification (length only); all gate outputs; deviations with rationale.

- Q1: [your question]

New feature request for the Plan section (E4's plan engine UI):

1. Interactive lever selection: user can select/toggle different levers (shop_insurance, trim_discretionary, defer_loan) and see runway gain/lose per lever combination — exploring how different levers impact the plan. Currently the ladder is a fixed ordered cumulative table (read-only rows with +N months). User wants selectable levers — i.e., pick a subset/order, see combined runway effect (and possibly lose? "gain/lose" — levers as modeled only gain; lose could come from... maybe a lever could be OFF vs ON baseline; or they imagine levers like "spend more on vacation" negative? More likely: see impact of each lever when toggled: baseline vs with-selected).

2. Remove/rework the "Backup: If the shock lands" section — redundant with the forecast (WeatherPanel shows shocked runway/landfall).

Design considerations:
- Lever model: currently leverLadder applies in fixed order cumulatively, each effect re-running runway. Interactive selection = a subset of available levers; combined effect = apply selected effects cumulatively (order per ladder order) and re-run runway once (or cumulative per selection change). The "+N months" = difference vs shocked baseline. Must keep invariant: every number = shocks.runway re-run (E4 acceptance). Selected-subset computation still satisfies that (sum deltas, one runway re-run — cumulative==sequential invariant already asserts final = single run over summed effects).
- Negative impact ("gain/lose"): with subset selection, deselecting shows loss vs all-on; or could show per-lever delta when toggled (marginal effect = with vs without that lever given others). Could also show a lever that hurts? All three levers only cut spending so they never reduce runway... but marginal can be +0.0 (trim then defer: trim +0, defer +3.2). Showing "no change" is honest. Where would "lose" come from? Maybe they imagine trade-offs (e.g. defer loan costs interest later — not modeled). We can show per-selection: total runway, per-lever marginal contribution (recomputed with others held), and honest caveats.
- UI: checkboxes/toggle chips per lever row; live recomputation; goal plan untouched; backup section removed (or replaced by the interactive plan? The "Backup: If the shock lands" is planText.backup lines — user says drop it since forecast covers it).

<subagent sessionID="ses_e44a229f6ffeBU7R2erXwtnCTA" state="completed" description="UI restyle: pixel art, light theme, map">
## QUESTIONS FOR USER

- Q1: `public/judge-sheet.html` (the printable judge sheet linked from the sticky bar) still carries its own near-black theme (`#070c18` ground). It was not in the stated light-theme scope (cp/wx/ax/jg/tailwind/component colors), so I left it. Convert it to the daylight palette too, or keep it as a dark print artifact?
- Q2: I committed the geometry generator at `scripts/map/build_district_geometry.py` (reproduces the committed asset byte for byte) so the fetch + simplify step is reproducible. Keep it, or drop it and treat the committed `src/assets/czechia-districts.ts` as the source of truth?

Best-effort answers used while you decide: Q1 left as-is (out of stated scope, reported below), Q2 kept (additive, outside `scripts/engine/*` and `scripts/analysis/*`, no gate impact).

---

## Frontend Implementation: Financial Resilience Engine UI pass

### Design Plan

- **Palette (6 named):** `#eaf1fb` Daylight ground · `#ffffff` Panel white · `#16273f` Slate ink · `#8496b3` Blueprint rule · `#0a7a5a` Provenance teal · `#8f5502` Ledger amber. Plus the five band hues kept as accents and re-tuned for AA: critical `#c02f12`, storm `#8f5502`, watch `#5744c2`, fair `#0b6b93`, clear `#0a7a5a`.
- **Typography:** display/utility = bundled **Silkscreen** (vendored OFL pixel face, chrome only: station title, eyebrows, section titles, band names, button caps); data = existing tabular mono stack (`ui-monospace`) for every number; body = system sans. Rationale: a scoreboard font must never change how a digit lines up, so pixels carry the chrome and mono carries the math.
- **Layout:** pixel sky band header (art bleeds full width, text sits on white plates) → console first (`lookup → baseline + shock → forecast → plan`) → Storm Atlas second → sticky JudgeBar → footer. ASCII: `[ PIXEL SKY + title plate + mascot ] / [ #console: lookup, baseline+shock, forecast, plan ] / [ #atlas: headline, gauge, map, strip ] / [ judge bar ] / [ footer ]`.
- **Signature element:** the **pixel sky header** that flips day to storm with the verdict band, with hard-chunk chrome (3px slate borders, zero radius, `Npx Npx 0 0` offset shadows, hard text-shadow readouts) everywhere else.

### Files per stage

| Stage | Files |
|---|---|
| 1 Light theme | `tailwind.config.js`, `src/index.css`, `src/components/weather/weather.css`, `src/components/judge/judge.css`, `src/components/atlas/atlas.css` |
| 2 Layout swap | `src/App.tsx`, `src/app.smoke.test.ts` |
| 3 Pixel art | new `src/components/sky/{PixelSky.tsx, PixelMascot.tsx, pixelGrid.tsx, sky.css, PixelSky.test.ts}`, new `src/assets/fonts/silkscreen-{400,700}.woff2`, `src/App.tsx` (header), `src/index.css` (font-face, chrome, readouts), `src/components/atlas/atlas.css`, `src/components/weather/weather.css`, `src/components/judge/judge.css` (chrome), `src/dashScan.test.ts` (AUTO_DIRS + CSS_FILES + coverage) |
| 4 Real map | new `src/assets/czechia-districts.ts`, new `src/lib/{districtNames.ts, districtNames.test.ts}`, new `scripts/map/build_district_geometry.py`, `src/components/atlas/{Cartogram.tsx, Cartogram.test.ts, atlas.css}`, `src/dashScan.test.ts` |
| 5 Gemini + gates | `src/state/consoleStore.ts`, `src/state/consoleStore.typed.test.ts` |

### Stage 1: light theme

Six named colors re-pointed at a daylight ground (`--rp-void` → `#eaf1fb`, `--rp-paper` → `#16273f` slate ink, panels now solid white instead of alpha-over-black). `--cp-inset` `rgba(7,12,24,.55)` → `#e6edf8`; all `wx-`, `jg-` hardcoded light-on-dark values swept; every band hue re-tuned; `::selection`, focus halo, slider thumb ink fixed where the old void token meant "dark ink". Tailwind `void/void-2/void-3/grid/ink/signal/cp` re-valued, so `App.tsx` classes needed no rewrite. `--rp-radius` → `0` and all pill radii → `0` for pixel corners.

### Stage 2: layout

`#console` now mounts above `#atlas`; both ids kept; `AtlasSection.handleSelectAccount` still scrolls to `#console` (now upward, `behavior: smooth|auto` from `prefersReducedMotion`, so no jarring jump). No test asserted the old order, so I **added** `app shell (layout order)` (document-order check via `compareDocumentPosition`, plus both slots and the drill target present) instead of leaving the contract unpinned.

### Stage 3: pixel art

- **Sky:** `PixelSky.tsx` draws a 320×32 rect grid (`shape-rendering: crispEdges`, `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMax slice"`), flat sky bands, stepped sun, block clouds with a shaded underside, staircase hills; storm scene swaps in indigo clouds, 16 stepped rain drops and a 4-block bolt. `min-height: clamp(120px,12vw,184px)` + centered plate keeps the horizon and sun in frame from 375px to 1920px.
- **Mascot:** `PixelMascot.tsx`, 32×32 grid, smiling cloud (ink outline, two eyes, three-block smile) over a gold-lidded coin jar with three square coins.
- **Motion:** rain falls in `steps(4)` whole-pixel jumps (8-unit loop = one drop, seamless), bolt flickers; both only inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, double-gated by the global reduce block.
- **Chrome:** 3px slate borders on panels/shell, 2px on controls, `box-shadow: Npx Npx 0 0` hard offsets only (verified: zero blurred shadows in live CSS), `text-shadow: 3px 3px 0 0` on runway/headline/gauge readouts (still `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`), `image-rendering: pixelated` on the header logo.
- **Font:** Silkscreen latin subset vendored to `src/assets/fonts/` (3,528 + 3,208 B, SIL OFL 1.1) and inlined as data URIs at build (both under Vite's 4,096 B inline limit), so runtime stays offline.
- No `public/art/` existed to remove (verified).

### Stage 4: cartogram as a real map

- **Source:** geoBoundaries **gbOpen CZE ADM2**, license **Public Domain**, 77 units, `boundaryCanonical: District`.
  API: `https://www.geoboundaries.org/api/current/gbOpen/CZE/ADM2/`
  File: `https://github.com/wmgeolab/geoBoundaries/raw/9469f09/releaseData/gbOpen/CZE/ADM2/geoBoundaries-CZE-ADM2_simplified.geojson`
- **Pipeline:** equirectangular projection with cos(lat) correction → Douglas-Peucker at 0.0025° (≈0.5 viewBox unit) → integer rounding on a `0 0 1000 572` grid (which is what gives the map the same chunky edge as the rest of the station) → `src/assets/czechia-districts.ts`.
- **Final size:** **78,085 bytes** (74,299 B of path data), 9,381 points, 77 paths. Well under the ~150 KB target. Generator committed at `scripts/map/build_district_geometry.py`; re-running it reproduces the committed body byte for byte.
- **Name match: 77/77, 0 unmatched, 0 orphan outlines.** Normalizer strips diacritics, collapses punctuation, drops leading `hl / hlavni / mesto / m` prefixes (`Hl.m. Praha` and `Hlavní město Praha` → `praha`), reads a lone `n` as `nad` (`Jablonec n. Nisou`), and an alias table maps the nine English geometry names (`Prague-East`, `Plzeň-City`, `Brno-Country`, `Ostrava-City` …) onto the CSV wording. Pinned permanently by `src/lib/districtNames.test.ts`, which reads `data/tangerine/districts.csv` and asserts every row joins and every outline is claimed. **Tile fallback is implemented and tested** (mixed fixture: 2 paths + 1 tile + the fallback legend sentence), just never triggered by shipped data.
- **Rendering:** one `<path>` per district, `role="button"`, `tabIndex=0`, full-sentence `aria-label` + `<title>` tooltip, Enter/Space activation, `data-district` / `data-bin` / `data-band` / `data-no-data` unchanged from the tile contract, shade via the same `color-mix(...32%...)` band mapping, hover and focus fill the full band color. `no_data` keeps a rotated hatch pattern path on top of its shade. A district with no counts takes **no shade** (white) so absent data never reads as a safe zero.
- **Tests:** `Cartogram.test.ts` 13 → **21**; existing coverage preserved (shading values, share + raw counts, no_data, click, inert, scenario label, legend, empty/refused states, SSR, gated-motion stylesheet) with copy assertions updated rather than dropped, plus 8 new map tests.

### Stage 5: Gemini fallback copy

`NOTE_NO_KEY` is now: **"Typed shocks run on a local build: npm run dev, or build and preview with .env. The deployed build falls back to preset cards."** No key hints, no secret names, honest about both paths. Test constant updated to match (assertion, not deletion).

**Key embedded verification (length only, value never printed):**
```json
{"keyPresent": true, "keyLength": 53, "keyNonEmpty": true, "assetFiles": 2, "embeddedInAssets": 1}
```

### Contrast ratios (band labels, WCAG AA = 4.5)

| Band label | on white panel | on inset `#e6edf8` | on ground `#eaf1fb` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical `#c02f12` | **5.74** | **4.88** | 5.05 |
| Storm warning `#8f5502` | **6.06** | **5.14** | 5.33 |
| Watch `#5744c2` | **6.97** | **5.92** | 6.14 |
| Fair skies `#0b6b93` | **5.93** | **5.04** | 5.22 |
| Clear `#0a7a5a` | **5.32** | **4.52** | 4.68 |

Body/labels: ink 13.23 (ground) / 15.04 (panel); dim `#3f5270` 6.97 / 7.92; faint `#56688a` 4.94 / 5.61 / 4.76 (inset). Derived alpha text: wx-dim 9.42, wx-faint 5.66, jg-dim 8.45, jg-faint 5.32 (all on white). White on critical chip 5.74, white on storm chip 6.06, keycap 11.93. **All ≥ 4.5.** Every verdict color still ships with glyph + label (VerdictBadge, WeatherBands, atlas cells, cartogram legend), so color never carries the verdict alone.

### Day/storm swap rule

`skyVariantFor(band)` in `PixelSky.tsx`: `critical` | `storm_warning` → **storm**; `watch` | `fair_skies` | `clear` | `null` (no account selected) → **day**. The live band is derived with the same two pure functions `ConsoleView` runs (`applyTwist` then `verdictBand`) over `bundle/selectedId/twist`, so the header cannot disagree with the badge. Pinned as a pure-function test and again end to end (Fair skies → day, `combo` → Storm warning → storm, `emergency_repair` → Critical → storm, reset → day).

### Gate outputs (final)

```
npx vitest run            Test Files  42 passed (42)
                          Tests       497 passed (497)        [was 474]
npm run typecheck         exit 0 (0 errors)
npm run build             exit 0, dist/assets/index.js 374.33 kB (gzip 120.70 kB)
                          index.css 78.32 kB (gzip 20.66 kB), 86 modules, ✓ built
uv run pytest -q          160 passed in 5.25s
uv run python -m scripts.engine.verify
                          drift: none (all accounts, all fields, atlas invariants, dash scan clean)
                          scripts.engine.verify: PASS
```

`dashScan.test.ts` green with `src/components/sky` in AUTO_DIRS, `sky.css` in CSS_FILES, and `src/assets/czechia-districts.ts` + `src/lib/districtNames{,.test}.ts` in EXPLICIT_FILES (coverage assertions added for all of them).

### Verification checklist

- [x] Design follows frontend-design skill (grounded in the subject, hero = the sky band, restraint everywhere else)
- [x] Distinctive, not templated (pixel weather station in daylight; no cream+serif+terracotta, no dark acid accent)
- [x] Responsive: header plate wraps, `clamp()` type, map `width:100%`, tiles already `auto-fit`, 44px targets kept
- [x] Visible keyboard focus: global `:focus-visible` ring (dark outline + blue halo), SVG paths get `outline: 3px` + 4px stroke
- [x] Reduced motion: global zeroing block + every new animation/transition gated behind `no-preference` (asserted from disk in both `PixelSky.test.ts` and the existing atlas stylesheet tests)
- [x] Accessibility: semantic `header/main/section/footer`, `aria-hidden` decorative art, `role="group"` map, `role="button"` paths with full-sentence labels, native `<title>` tooltips, glyph+label with every band color
- [x] No em/en dashes, minus signs, double or spaced hyphens in any new string, comment, or CSS prose (dashScan + engine dash scan clean; the only ` - ` hits are arithmetic subtraction in code, which the rule explicitly allows)
- [x] Build succeeds; all five gates green
- [x] Integer cents / zero money math in components / single band vocabulary in `src/lib/verdict.ts` — untouched
- [x] Runtime offline: only `profiles.json` + `atlas.json` fetches; geometry and font are bundled
- [x] Untouched as required: `scripts/engine/*`, `scripts/analysis/*`, `docs/devpost.md`, `docs/video/*`, README.md, `.github/*`, `consoleStore` behavior (only the one note string), judge key semantics

### Deviations, with rationale

1. **Vendored a pixel font** (allowed by the brief: "only if you can vendor it offline"). Silkscreen, SIL OFL 1.1, 6.7 KB total, latin subset, inlined as data URIs so it costs zero runtime requests. Chrome only; all numerals stay tabular mono.
2. **`public/judge-sheet.html` left dark** — outside the stated token scope (see Q1). It is a standalone print artifact with its own inline styles.
3. **Dead report CSS left in place.** `grep` shows `.rp-report` / `.rv-*` blocks are referenced by no component (only `rp-sr-only` is used) and `judge-sheet.html` has its own styles. I retuned the `--rp-*` tokens they depend on (so nothing reads dark) but did not delete ~1,200 lines of unused CSS, since that was outside the brief. The two remaining dark literals are inside those dead blocks.
4. **Generator committed** under `scripts/map/` (see Q2); it is additive and outside the off-limits `scripts/engine/*` and `scripts/analysis/*`.
5. **Region tile grid retained as the fallback surface** rather than removed, so districts the geometry does not know stay visible, keyboard reachable, and covered by the existing tests.
6. **Concurrent session note:** `README.md` and `docs/decisions.md` show as modified in `git status`. Those edits are **not mine** (another session is writing a "Phase E8: Lever explorer" record; its own note references coordinating with "the concurrent UI restyle"). I did not read-modify-write either file. All of my changes are listed in the per-stage table above.
</subagent>

Plus the five band hues kept as accents and re-tuned for AA: critical `#c02f12`, storm `#8f5502`, watch `#5744c2`, fair `#0b6b93`, clear `#0a7a5a`.
- **Typography:** display/utility = bundled **Silkscreen** (vendored OFL pixel face, chrome only: station title, eyebrows, section titles, band names, button caps); data = existing tabular mono stack (`ui-monospace`) for every number; body = system sans. Rationale: a scoreboard font must never change how a digit lines up, so pixels carry the chrome and mono carries the math.
- **Layout:** pixel sky band header (art bleeds full width, text sits on white plates) → console first (`lookup → baseline + shock → forecast → plan`) → Storm Atlas second → sticky JudgeBar → footer. ASCII: `[ PIXEL SKY + title plate + mascot ] / [ #console: lookup, baseline+shock, forecast, plan ] / [ #atlas: headline, gauge, map, strip ] / [ judge bar ] / [ footer ]`.
- **Signature element:** the **pixel sky header** that flips day to storm with the verdict band, with hard-chunk chrome (3px slate borders, zero radius, `Npx Npx 0 0` offset shadows, hard text-shadow readouts) everywhere else.

| Stage | Files |
|---|---|
| 1 Light theme | `tailwind.config.js`, `src/index.css`, `src/components/weather/weather.css`, `src/components/judge/judge.css`, `src/components/atlas/atlas.css` |
| 2 Layout swap | `src/App.tsx`, `src/app.smoke.test.ts` |
| 3 Pixel art | new `src/components/sky/{PixelSky.tsx, PixelMascot.tsx, pixelGrid.tsx, sky.css, PixelSky.test.ts}`, new `src/assets/fonts/silkscreen-{400,700}.woff2`, `src/App.tsx` (header), `src/index.css` (font-face, chrome, readouts), `src/components/atlas/atlas.css`, `src/components/weather/weather.css`, `src/components/judge/judge.css` (chrome), `src/dashScan.test.ts` (AUTO_DIRS + CSS_FILES + coverage) |
| 4 Real map | new `src/assets/czechia-districts.ts`, new `src/lib/{districtNames.ts, districtNames.test.ts}`, new `scripts/map/build_district_geometry.py`, `src/components/atlas/{Cartogram.tsx, Cartogram.test.ts, atlas.css}`, `src/dashScan.test.ts` |
| 5 Gemini + gates | `src/state/consoleStore.ts`, `src/state/consoleStore.typed.test.ts` |

### Stage 1: light theme

Six named colors re-pointed at a daylight ground (`--rp-void` → `#eaf1fb`, `--rp-paper` → `#16273f` slate ink, panels now solid white instead of alpha-over-black). `--cp-inset` `rgba(7,12,24,.55)` → `#e6edf8`; all `wx-`, `jg-` hardcoded light-on-dark values swept; every band hue re-tuned; `::selection`, focus halo, slider thumb ink fixed where the old void token meant "dark ink". Tailwind `void/void-2/void-3/grid/ink/signal/cp` re-valued, so `App.tsx` classes needed no rewrite. `--rp-radius` → `0` and all pill radii → `0` for pixel corners.

### Stage 2: layout

`#console` now mounts above `#atlas`; both ids kept; `AtlasSection.handleSelectAccount` still scrolls to `#console` (now upward, `behavior: smooth|auto` from `prefersReducedMotion`, so no jarring jump). No test asserted the old order, so I **added** `app shell (layout order)` (document-order check via `compareDocumentPosition`, plus both slots and the drill target present) instead of leaving the contract unpinned.

### Stage 3: pixel art

- **Sky:** `PixelSky.tsx` draws a 320×32 rect grid (`shape-rendering: crispEdges`, `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMax slice"`), flat sky bands, stepped sun, block clouds with a shaded underside, staircase hills; storm scene swaps in indigo clouds, 16 stepped rain drops and a 4-block bolt. `min-height: clamp(120px,12vw,184px)` + centered plate keeps the horizon and sun in frame from 375px to 1920px.
- **Mascot:** `PixelMascot.tsx`, 32×32 grid, smiling cloud (ink outline, two eyes, three-block smile) over a gold-lidded coin jar with three square coins.
- **Motion:** rain falls in `steps(4)` whole-pixel jumps (8-unit loop = one drop, seamless), bolt flickers; both only inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, double-gated by the global reduce block.
- **Chrome:** 3px slate borders on panels/shell, 2px on controls, `box-shadow: Npx Npx 0 0` hard offsets only (verified: zero blurred shadows in live CSS), `text-shadow: 3px 3px 0 0` on runway/headline/gauge readouts (still `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`), `image-rendering: pixelated` on the header logo.
- **Font:** Silkscreen latin subset vendored to `src/assets/fonts/` (3,528 + 3,208 B, SIL OFL 1.1) and inlined as data URIs at build (both under Vite's 4,096 B inline limit), so runtime stays offline.
- No `public/art/` existed to remove (verified).

### Stage 4: cartogram as a real map

- **Source:** geoBoundaries **gbOpen CZE ADM2**, license **Public Domain**, 77 units, `boundaryCanonical: District`.
  API: `https://www.geoboundaries.org/api/current/gbOpen/CZE/ADM2/`
  File: `https://github.com/wmgeolab/geoBoundaries/raw/9469f09/releaseData/gbOpen/CZE/ADM2/geoBoundaries-CZE-ADM2_simplified.geojson`
- **Pipeline:** equirectangular projection with cos(lat) correction → Douglas-Peucker at 0.0025° (≈0.5 viewBox unit) → integer rounding on a `0 0 1000 572` grid (which is what gives the map the same chunky edge as the rest of the station) → `src/assets/czechia-districts.ts`.
- **Final size:** **78,085 bytes** (74,299 B of path data), 9,381 points, 77 paths. Well under the ~150 KB target. Generator committed at `scripts/map/build_district_geometry.py`; re-running it reproduces the committed body byte for byte.
- **Name match: 77/77, 0 unmatched, 0 orphan outlines.** Normalizer strips diacritics, collapses punctuation, drops leading `hl / hlavni / mesto / m` prefixes (`Hl.m. Praha` and `Hlavní město Praha` → `praha`), reads a lone `n` as `nad` (`Jablonec n. Nisou`), and an alias table maps the nine English geometry names (`Prague-East`, `Plzeň-City`, `Brno-Country`, `Ostrava-City` …) onto the CSV wording. Pinned permanently by `src/lib/districtNames.test.ts`, which reads `data/tangerine/districts.csv` and asserts every row joins and every outline is claimed. **Tile fallback is implemented and tested** (mixed fixture: 2 paths + 1 tile + the fallback legend sentence), just never triggered by shipped data.
- **Rendering:** one `<path>` per district, `role="button"`, `tabIndex=0`, full-sentence `aria-label` + `<title>` tooltip, Enter/Space activation, `data-district` / `data-bin` / `data-band` / `data-no-data` unchanged from the tile contract, shade via the same `color-mix(...32%...)` band mapping, hover and focus fill the full band color. `no_data` keeps a rotated hatch pattern path on top of its shade. A district with no counts takes **no shade** (white) so absent data never reads as a safe zero.
- **Tests:** `Cartogram.test.ts` 13 → **21**; existing coverage preserved (shading values, share + raw counts, no_data, click, inert, scenario label, legend, empty/refused states, SSR, gated-motion stylesheet) with copy assertions updated rather than dropped, plus 8 new map tests.

### Stage 5: Gemini fallback copy

`NOTE_NO_KEY` is now: **"Typed shocks run on a local build: npm run dev, or build and preview with .env. The deployed build falls back to preset cards."** No key hints, no secret names, honest about both paths. Test constant updated to match (assertion, not deletion).

| Band label | on white panel | on inset `#e6edf8` | on ground `#eaf1fb` |

| Critical `#c02f12` | **5.74** | **4.88** | 5.05 |

Derived alpha text: wx-dim 9.42, wx-faint 5.66, jg-dim 8.45, jg-faint 5.32 (all on white). `skyVariantFor(band)` in `PixelSky.tsx`: `critical` | `storm_warning` → **storm**; `watch` | `fair_skies` | `clear` | `null` (no account selected) → **day**. | Check | Verdict | Details |
|-------|---------|---------|
| 1. consoleStore note only | PASS | `git diff HEAD -- src/state/consoleStore.ts` is exactly one hunk: the `NOTE_NO_KEY` string at consoleStore.ts:116 (`'Gemini key not configured, using preset cards'` → `'Typed shocks run on a local build: npm run dev, or build and preview with .env. The deployed build falls back to preset cards.'`). Key semantics (generation counter :149-159, preset match :106-113, typed lifecycle :255-324) byte identical; consoleStore.typed.test.ts changed +1/-1 to pin the same literal (:118, asserted :197, :210-219) |
| 2. Layout: console above atlas | PASS | `#console` at App.tsx:60 mounts above `#atlas` at App.tsx:63, both ids present; atlas drill scrolls via `getElementById('console')` + `scrollIntoView` (AtlasSection.tsx:159-163, tested AtlasSection.test.ts:183-239); order test is meaningful (app.smoke.test.ts:153-175 uses `compareDocumentPosition`, asserts both slots and the scroll target); row click scoped to `#console` (:138), closing the prior E5 low |
| 3. Light theme sweep | PASS | Zero hits for `#070c18`, `#0d1526`, `#e9effa` in all of src; judge.css/weather.css/index.css token blocks are daylight values, atlas.css has no raw hex. No blurred box-shadows: every `box-shadow` is zero-blur offset or ring (weather.css:228 multiline is `3px 3px 0 0` + inset). Dead CSS verified genuinely dead (see judgment below). One residual outside the sweep: `#070c18` at public/judge-sheet.html:13,19 (flagged Low) |
| 4. Pixel art integrity | PASS | Derivation uses the same pure functions as ConsoleView (PixelSky.tsx:168-181 `applyTwist` then `verdictBand(runway)` vs ConsoleView.tsx:57-58; no second path). Storm only for `critical|storm_warning` (PixelSky.tsx:35-40, pinned PixelSky.test.ts:85-97). Motion double-gated (sky.css:95-103 `no-preference` gate + index.css:113-125 global reduce zeroing; asserted PixelSky.test.ts:198-214). `aria-hidden` + `focusable="false"` on both SVGs (PixelSky.tsx:202-203, PixelMascot.tsx:67-68). Font attribution present (index.css:5-12) |
| 5. Map | PASS | Geometry bundled, exactly 78,085 B (wc -c, matches claim), 77 entries + `CZECHIA_DISTRICT_COUNT` guard (czechia-districts.ts:205-210, pinned districtNames.test.ts:72-83); name-match test reads real data/tangerine/districts.csv (77 rows) and pins 77/77 both directions (districtNames.test.ts:85-104); zero fetch in Cartogram/assets (only bundled JSON loads + gated Gemini call remain in src); `data-bin`/`data-band` + click kept (Cartogram.tsx:145-146, 188-189, tested Cartogram.test.ts:215-231, 310-335); no_data hatch (Cartogram.tsx:157-164, tested :357-377) with corrected legend wording (:333, closing the prior Medium); keyboard `role="button"` `tabIndex={0}` Enter/Space (Cartogram.tsx:133-138, 149-150); tile fallback tested (Cartogram.test.ts:434-450) |
| 6. Gemini note + no key material | PASS | New copy pinned identically in store (:116) and test (consoleStore.typed.test.ts:118, asserted :197). No AIza-style or long secret literal in any file; `.env` gitignored (gitignore:47) and untracked (`git ls-files .env` empty); only `VITE_GEMINI_KEY` name references. Key is not in any committed file |
| 7. Content rule / dashScan | PASS | dashScan green inside the 497 run; every new/modified file registered (dashScan.test.ts:42, 47-48, 82, 87-94, coverage asserts :259-267). Independent grep sweep over sky/, districtNames pair, czechia-districts.ts, Cartogram pair, scripts/map, and all 10 modified files: zero em/en/minus/spaced-hyphen prose. Five-cycle registry-lag pattern finally closed |
| 8. Integer cents / single vocabulary | PASS | PixelSky holds zero money math; Cartogram reads precomputed BandCounts, display percent only via `roundHalfUp` (Cartogram.tsx:111), no cents/runway math; band ids only from verdict.ts through `bandForBin`. The `day`/`storm` scene words are art directions keyed off `verdictBand`, not a second state vocabulary |
| 9. Gates | PASS | vitest 42 files / 497 tests (exact brief counts), typecheck exit 0, build exit 0 (86 modules), pytest 160 passed, scripts.engine.verify PASS, sha256 `9ec428bf...c40a858` unchanged; gate runs left the tree byte identical |
| 10. Vendored font | PASS | Two valid WOFF2 (3,528 B / 3,208 B), both under the 4 kB inline limit, confirmed inlined as `data:font/woff2;base64` in dist/assets/index-CsXnQf2j.css; only relative `url()` refs (index.css:19, 27); zero external font fetches. Files present in the change set (untracked like all stage 3/4 additions; include in the commit) |

### Findings (non-blocking)

| Severity | File:Line | Issue | Suggested Fix |
|----------|-----------|-------|---------------|
| Low | src/index.css:5-12 | Attribution note names Silkscreen, Jason Kottke, SIL OFL 1.1, but no LICENSE/OFL.txt ships with the vendored woff2 binaries anywhere in the repo; OFL 1.1 §1 expects the license text to accompany redistributed font files | Add src/assets/fonts/OFL.txt and cite it from the header |
| Low | src/index.css:131, 1293-1598 | Dead `.rp-report`/`.rv-*` blocks verified unreferenced but still ship ~300 dead lines in the 78.32 kB CSS bundle | Delete in a cleanup pass |
| Low | public/judge-sheet.html:13,19 | Old dark literal `#070c18` survives on a live surface (JudgeBar paper sheet link) outside the declared sweep list | Retheme to daylight tokens or record the dark sheet as intentional in docs/decisions.md |
| Low | src/components/atlas/Cartogram.test.ts:379-401 | Keyboard access pinned for Enter only; Space branch (Cartogram.tsx:134) untested | Add one Space assertion beside Enter |

### Requested Judgments

- **Dead-CSS decision: ACCEPTED.** Grep over ts/tsx/js/html/py/md finds zero references to any `.rp-report` or `.rv-*` selector outside the stylesheet (only prose at docs/reviews.md-referenced docs/research.md:1807); the consuming components were deleted in the Tier B cleanup (App.tsx:23-24). Deferral is honest; residual cost is bundle weight only (Low 2).
- **Font license attribution: contract satisfied as worded, weak on OFL hygiene.** The contract asks for "a LICENSE or attribution note"; index.css:5-12 is a proper attribution note (face, author, license named). However, redistributing OFL binaries without the license text is the weaker reading of OFL 1.1, hence Low 1.

- [x] All ten contract checks passed
- [x] No critical or medium issues found
- [x] Code follows project conventions (single store, pure lib functions, five-band vocabulary, dash rule)
- [x] No em dashes, double hyphens, or dash equivalents in any new or modified file (independent sweep + dashScan)
- [x] Phase code integrates cleanly with prior phases (closes prior review lows at reviews.md:207 row-click scoping and the cartogram legend Medium)
- [x] Out-of-scope noise flagged, not failed: README.md (20 lines) and docs/decisions.md (+33) dirty from a concurrent session; docs/devpost.md clean against HEAD
- [x] Findings appended to docs/reviews.md (verified: additions only at file tail)

One scope note: the stage table lists Cartogram.tsx and its test as NEW, but git shows them as modified on top of the E5 tile cartogram (the map rewrite supersedes it in place; diffs and tests are internally consistent). Not a defect, recorded for provenance clarity.
